dr_terms: The sceptre (*sceptrum*) shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler (*dux*) from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.
dr_plain: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.
vulgate_text: Non auferetur sceptrum de Iuda, et dux de femore eius, donec veniat qui mittendus est, et ipse erit expectatio gentium.
locus: ST III, q. 31, a. 2; Super Is., cap. 11; Super Io., cap. 1, l. 14.
lit_eng: Jacob prophesies the continuity of the civil and judicial sceptre of Judah until the historical advent of the Messiah.
spi_eng: The cessation of the earthly sceptre signifies the transition from the temporal Old Law to the universal spiritual kingdom of Christ among all Gentile nations.
lit_lat: «Prophetia de cessatione regni et principatus Iudaeorum adveniente Christo» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Per sceptrum intelligitur regnum spirituale Christi extendendum ad gentes» (*Super Io.*, cap. 1, l. 14).

dr_terms: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever (*Dominus regnabit in aeternum et ultra*).
dr_plain: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.
vulgate_text: Dominus regnabit in aeternum et ultra.
locus: Super Ps. 9, n. 4; Super Ps. 28, n. 4; ST I, q. 103, a. 1.
lit_eng: Moses celebrates YHWH's sovereign victory over Pharaoh's hosts at the Red Sea as proof of His perpetual kingship.
spi_eng: The Red Sea prefigures Baptism, following which God establishes His everlasting kingdom over the elect in eternal beatitude.
lit_lat: «Dominus regnat per essentiam et gubernationem ab aeterno et in saeculum» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Transitus maris rubri est figura Baptismi, post quem Deus regnat in electis in aeternum» (*Super Ps.* 9, n. 4).

dr_terms: And you shall be to me a priestly kingdom (*regnum sacerdotale*), and a holy nation (*gens sancta*).
dr_plain: And you shall be to me a priestly kingdom, and a holy nation.
vulgate_text: Vos eritis mihi in regnum sacerdotale, et gens sancta.
locus: ST I-II, q. 104, a. 1, ad 1; ST III, q. 22, a. 1, ad 3.
lit_eng: God constitutes the historical commonwealth of Israel as a dedicated theocracy under the Sinai covenant.
spi_eng: Prefigures the Church Militant of the New Law, where all the baptized participate sacramentally in Christ's eternal royal priesthood (*regnum sacerdotale*).
lit_lat: «Populus carnaliter Deo consecratus sub veteri lege per ministerium iudiciale» (*ST* I-II, q. 104, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Figura regalis sacerdotii Novi Testamenti, ubi omnes fideles spiritualiter sunt sacerdotes et reges» (*ST* III, q. 22, a. 1, ad 3).

dr_terms: The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king (*clangor victoriae regis*) in him.
dr_plain: The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him.
vulgate_text: Dominus Deus eius cum eo est, et clangor victoriae regis in illo.
locus: ST I-II, q. 102, a. 4; Super Ps. 46, n. 2.
lit_eng: Balaam confesses that YHWH is present as the supreme royal Leader and Victor among the camps of Israel.
spi_eng: Signifies the indwelling of God in the soul of the just, whose grace grants continuous triumph over the assaults of demonic powers.
lit_lat: «Praesentia Dei ut regis et protectoris in castris Israel ad victoriam temporalem» (*ST* I-II, q. 102, a. 4).
spi_lat: «Clangor victoriae regis est vox gratiae in corde iusti super daemones triumphans» (*Super Ps.* 46, n. 2).

dr_terms: He shall be king (*rex*) with the most right, the princes of the people being assembled with the tribes of Israel.
dr_plain: He shall be king with the most right, the princes of the people being assembled with the tribes of Israel.
vulgate_text: Erit apud rectissimum rex, congregatis principibus populi cum tribubus Israel.
locus: ST I-II, q. 105, a. 1.
lit_eng: God is proclaimed the supreme legislative King of Jeshurun, establishing an optimal mixed regime under divine law.
spi_eng: Typifies Christ the supreme Lawgiver assembling the princes of the Church and all peoples into the unity of faith.
lit_lat: «Optima ordinatio principum sub Deo rege supremo in populo Israel» (*ST* I-II, q. 105, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Figura Christi qui congregat principes Ecclesiae et tribus omnium gentium sub una lege Evangelii» (*ST* I-II, q. 105, a. 1).

dr_terms: Gedeon said to them: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you, but the Lord shall rule over you (*sed dominabitur vobis Dominus*).
dr_plain: Gedeon said to them: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you, but the Lord shall rule over you.
vulgate_text: Dixitque eis Gedeon: Non dominabor vestri, nec dominabitur in vos filius meus, sed dominabitur vobis Dominus.
locus: ST I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2; De reg. I, cap. 2.
lit_eng: Gideon rejects hereditary human monarchy, maintaining the unmediated theocratic sovereignty of YHWH over Israel.
spi_eng: The human will must remain subject immediately to divine rule, refusing to allow created appetites or vices to exercise dominion over the soul.
lit_lat: «Gedeon recusavit dominatum, asserens solum Deum debere immediate populo imperare» (*ST* I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2).
spi_lat: «Anima debet soli Deo subesse, ne peccatum aut creatura in ea dominetur» (*De reg.* I, cap. 2).

dr_terms: And the Lord said to Samuel: Hearken to the voice of the people in all that they say to thee. For they have not rejected thee, but me, that I should not reign over them (*ne regnem super eos*).
dr_plain: And the Lord said to Samuel: Hearken to the voice of the people in all that they say to thee. For they have not rejected thee, but me, that I should not reign over them.
vulgate_text: Dixit autem Dominus ad Samuelem: Audi vocem populi in omnibus quae loquuntur tibi: non enim te abiecerunt, sed me, ne regnem super eos.
locus: ST I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2; De reg. I, cap. 1.
lit_eng: Israel's sin was desiring an earthly king after the manner of the Gentiles, thereby discounting God's immediate royal protection.
spi_eng: Prefigures the human soul defecting from the gentle internal governance of grace to seek external, perishable consolations.
lit_lat: «Peccaverunt petendo regem ad modum gentium, quasi diffidentes de divina providentia et regimine» (*ST* I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2).
spi_lat: «Apostasia voluntatis a regimine divino ad dominatum carnalem et saecularem» (*De reg.* I, cap. 1).

dr_terms: You said to me: Nay, but a king shall reign over us (*rex imperabit nobis*): whereas the Lord your God was your king (*cum Dominus Deus vester regnaret in vobis*).
dr_plain: You said to me: Nay, but a king shall reign over us: whereas the Lord your God was your king.
vulgate_text: Dixistis mihi: Nequaquam, sed rex imperabit nobis: cum Dominus Deus vester regnaret in vobis.
locus: ST I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2; Super I Cor., cap. 15, l. 3.
lit_eng: Samuel rebukes Israel's lack of faith during Nahash's invasion, recalling that God Himself was their true King.
spi_eng: Rebukes the believer who relies upon secular power or carnal strength in spiritual warfare instead of the Lord.
lit_lat: «Redargutio populi quia potius voluerunt regi ab homine mortali quam a Deo immortali» (*ST* I-II, q. 105, a. 1, ad 2).
spi_lat: «Omnis humana potestas deficit nisi a divino regimine sustinetur» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 15, l. 3).

dr_terms: I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever (*firmabo thronum regni eius usque in sempiternum*)... And thy house shall be firm, and thy kingdom for ever (*regnum tuum usque in sempiternum*) before thy face, and thy throne shall be firm for ever.
dr_plain: I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever... And thy house shall be firm, and thy kingdom for ever before thy face, and thy throne shall be firm for ever.
vulgate_text: Et firmabo thronum regni eius usque in sempiternum... et firmabitur domus tua, et regnum tuum usque in sempiternum coram facie tua, et thronus tuus erit firmus iugiter.
locus: ST III, q. 31, a. 2; ST III, q. 59, a. 2; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 3; Super Ps. 88, n. 4.
lit_eng: The Nathan oracle promises an enduring dynasty; because Solomon's earthly kingdom fell, Thomas states the literal sense intended by the Holy Spirit terminates strictly in Christ (*sensus litteralis propheticus*).
spi_eng: The throne of Christ established permanently in the faithful soul by charity, perfected in the eternal kingdom of glory.
lit_lat: «Litteraliter de Christo intelligitur: regnum enim Salomonis non fuit in sempiternum firmum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Thronus eius aeternus firmatur in cordibus fidelium per gratiam, et in beatis per gloriam» (*Super Ps.* 88, n. 4).

dr_terms: And Solomon sat upon the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was strengthened exceedingly (*firmatum est regnum eius nimis*).
dr_plain: And Solomon sat upon the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was strengthened exceedingly.
vulgate_text: Sedit autem Salomon super thronum David patris sui, et firmatum est regnum eius nimis.
locus: ST III, q. 31, a. 2; Super Ps. 71, n. 1.
lit_eng: Solomon succeeds David and his temporal monarchy is firmly established in Jerusalem.
spi_eng: Solomon (*Rex Pacificus*) typifies Christ the Prince of Peace, whose spiritual kingdom is consolidated through the Cross and Resurrection.
lit_lat: «Salomon sedit in throno David et pacificatum est regnum eius in Ierusalem» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Salomon, idest pacificus, est figura Christi regnantis in pace Ecclesiae suae» (*Super Ps.* 71, n. 1).

dr_terms: And I will settle him in my house, and in my kingdom for ever (*in regno meo usque in sempiternum*): and his throne shall be most firm for ever.
dr_plain: And I will settle him in my house, and in my kingdom for ever: and his throne shall be most firm for ever.
vulgate_text: Sed statuam eum in domo mea, et in regno meo usque in sempiternum: et thronus eius erit firmissimus in perpetuum.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Paralipomenon).
lit_eng: God promises to confirm the Davidic king directly within His own house and kingdom forever.
spi_eng: Identifies the Davidic kingdom with God's own divine kingdom, realized eternally in Christ's headship over the Church.
lit_lat: «Deus regnum Davidicum vocat regnum suum, perpetuo stabiliendum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Christus secundum humanitatem constituitur caput regni divini in aeternum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: He hath chosen Solomon my son, to sit for a king upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord (*in throno regni Domini*) over Israel.
dr_plain: He hath chosen Solomon my son, to sit for a king upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
vulgate_text: Elegit Salomonem filium meum, ut sederet in throno regni Domini super Israel.
locus: ST I-II, q. 105, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 14. (Nullus commentarius directus in Paralipomenon).
lit_eng: David designates the historical throne of Jerusalem as 'the throne of the kingdom of the Lord'.
spi_eng: Prefigures the visible hierarchy and pastoral authority of the Church Militant, who govern as vicars of Christ's kingdom.
lit_lat: «Thronus regni terreni dicitur thronus regni Domini, quia rex erat minister Dei» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).
spi_lat: «Figura visibilis regiminis Ecclesiae, ubi praelati loco Christi vices eius gerunt» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: Thine, O Lord, is magnificence, and power, and glory, and victory... thine, O Lord, is the kingdom (*tuum Domine regnum*), and thou art above all princes.
dr_plain: Thine, O Lord, is magnificence, and power, and glory, and victory... thine, O Lord, is the kingdom, and thou art above all princes.
vulgate_text: Tua est enim Domine magnificentia, et potentia, et gloria, atque victoria... tuum Domine regnum, et tu es super omnes principes.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 1; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: David's solemn liturgical doxology professing God's essential, uncreated kingship and dominion over all created rulers.
spi_eng: Foretastes the eternal liturgy of heaven, where all glorified creatures render homage to God as the sole supreme Lord.
lit_lat: «Tuum est regnum: professio divini dominii super omnem creaturam et super omnes principes» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «In caelis perfecte manifestabitur hoc regnum quando Deus erit omnia in omnibus» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: And now you say that you are able to withstand the kingdom of the Lord (*regno Domini*), which he possesseth by the sons of David...
dr_plain: And now you say that you are able to withstand the kingdom of the Lord, which he possesseth by the sons of David...
vulgate_text: Nunc ergo vos dicitis quod resistere possitis regno Domini, quod possidet per filios David.
locus: ST II-II, q. 10, a. 10. (Nullus commentarius directus in Paralipomenon).
lit_eng: Abijah defends the legitimate covenantal monarchy of the house of David against the schismatic revolt of Jeroboam.
spi_eng: Prefigures the unity and indefectibility of the Catholic Church against heretical sects that attempt to overthrow divine apostolic authority.
lit_lat: «Defensio legitimae successionis Davidicae contra schisma Ieroboam» (*ST* II-II, q. 10, a. 10).
spi_lat: «Unitas regni Ecclesiae sub legitimis pastoribus contra haereticorum et schismaticorum rebellionem» (*ST* II-II, q. 10, a. 10).

dr_terms: O Lord God of our fathers, thou art God in heaven, and rulest over all the kingdoms and nations (*dominaris omnibus regnis gentium*)...
dr_plain: O Lord God of our fathers, thou art God in heaven, and rulest over all the kingdoms and nations...
vulgate_text: Domine Deus patrum nostrorum, tu es Deus in caelo, et dominaris omnibus regnis gentium.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 3. (Nullus commentarius directus in Paralipomenon).
lit_eng: King Jehoshaphat appeals in prayer to God's universal providence governing all pagan realms and empires.
spi_eng: The soul threatened by spiritual enemies finds peace in the certitude that God holds absolute dominion over all hostile powers.
lit_lat: «Divina dominatio et gubernatio immediate extenditur super omnia regna gentium» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 3).
spi_lat: «Securitas animae orantis, scientis nihil in mundo accidere posse extra divinam providentiam» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 3).

dr_terms: He will not take away his eyes from the just, and he placeth kings on the throne for ever (*reges in solio collocat in perpetuum*), and they are exalted.
dr_plain: He will not take away his eyes from the just, and he placeth kings on the throne for ever, and they are exalted.
vulgate_text: Non auferet a iusto oculos suos, et reges in solio collocat in perpetuum, et illi eriguntur.
locus: Super Iob, cap. 36, l. 1.
lit_eng: Elihu explains that divine providence never loses sight of the righteous, elevating them to royal honor.
spi_eng: God grants the just interior spiritual dominion over their passions in this life, and seats them upon everlasting thrones of heavenly glory.
lit_lat: «Iustos Deus nunquam deserit, sed facit eos participes regiae dignitatis» (*Super Iob*, cap. 36, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Reges sunt iusti qui regunt motus carnis in praesenti, et collocantur in solio gloriae in perpetuum» (*Super Iob*, cap. 36, l. 1).

dr_terms: But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain (*Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion*), preaching his commandment. The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee. Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance...
dr_plain: But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, preaching his commandment. The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee. Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance...
vulgate_text: Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, praedicans praeceptum eius. Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te. Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes haereditatem tuam...
locus: Super Ps. 2, nn. 4–6; ST III, q. 59, a. 1; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 2.
lit_eng: In Thomas's exegesis, the literal prophetic sense refers immediately to Christ constituted King over Mount Zion in His human nature, receiving the Gentiles into His Church.
spi_eng: The spiritual enthronement of Christ on the 'holy mountain' of the believer's purified soul, which He rules through His divine precepts.
lit_lat: «Litteraliter de Christo: constitutus est rex a Patre secundum humanam naturam super Sion, idest super Ecclesiam» (*Super Ps.* 2, n. 4).
spi_lat: «Sion, quae speculatio interpretatur, est anima contemplativa in qua Christus regnat per fidem formatam» (*Super Ps.* 2, n. 4).

dr_terms: And the Lord remaineth for ever. He hath prepared his throne in judgment (*paravit in iudicio thronum suum*): and he shall judge the world in equity...
dr_plain: And the Lord remaineth for ever. He hath prepared his throne in judgment: and he shall judge the world in equity...
vulgate_text: Et Dominus in aeternum permanet. Paravit in iudicio thronum suum: et ipse iudicabit orbem terrae in aequitate...
locus: Super Ps. 9, nn. 7–8; ST III, q. 59, a. 1.
lit_eng: The Lord's unshakeable throne is established from eternity to execute righteous judgment over the nations.
spi_eng: The final judicial tribunal of Christ at the Parousia, where the hidden deeds of all men are judged with absolute rectitude.
lit_lat: «Thronus iudiciariae potestatis paratus est ad iudicandum orbem in aequitate» (*Super Ps.* 9, n. 7).
spi_lat: «Thronus iste manifestabitur in novissimo die quando Christus visibiliter veniet omnia iudicare» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).

dr_terms: The Lord shall reign to eternity (*Dominus regnabit in aeternum*), yea, for ever and ever: ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.
dr_plain: The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.
vulgate_text: Dominus regnabit in aeternum, et in saeculum saeculi: peribitis gentes de terra illius.
locus: Super Ps. 9 (LXX 9b/10), n. 16.
lit_eng: YHWH's perpetual kingship destroys idolatrous pagan nations from the sacred territory of Israel.
spi_eng: The destruction of carnal vices from the soul, and the final purification of the Church from all hypocrites and unrepentant sinners.
lit_lat: «Regnum Domini manet aeternum per exterminium infidelium de terra promissa» (*Super Ps.* 9, n. 16).
spi_lat: «Peribunt gentes, idest carnales affectus et vitia, de anima quae est terra sancta Dei» (*Super Ps.* 9, n. 16).

dr_terms: For the kingdom is the Lord's (*quoniam Domini est regnum*); and he shall have dominion over the nations (*ipse dominabitur gentium*).
dr_plain: For the kingdom is the Lord's; and he shall have dominion over the nations.
vulgate_text: Quoniam Domini est regnum: et ipse dominabitur gentium.
locus: Super Ps. 21, n. 28; ST III, q. 49, a. 6.
lit_eng: Universal sovereignty belongs naturally to YHWH, before whom all the families of the nations must bow.
spi_eng: Thomas shows that Christ's universal kingship over the Gentiles is the direct fruit and merit of His Passion and death upon the Cross.
lit_lat: «Deo competit universale dominium super omnes populos terrae» (*Super Ps.* 21, n. 28).
spi_lat: «Fructus passionis Christi est conversio gentium ad regnum et dominium eius» (*ST* III, q. 49, a. 6).

dr_terms: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory (*rex gloriae*) shall enter in. Who is this King of Glory? The Lord who is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.
dr_plain: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory shall enter in. Who is this King of Glory? The Lord who is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.
vulgate_text: Attollite portas principes vestras, et elevamini portae aeternales: et introibit rex gloriae. Quis est iste rex gloriae? Dominus fortis et potens: Dominus potens in praelio.
locus: Super Ps. 23, n. 7; ST III, q. 57, a. 6; In Sym., a. 6.
lit_eng: Liturgical entry of the Ark of the Covenant through the gates of Jerusalem.
spi_eng: The triumphant bodily Ascension of Christ the Victorious King, before whom the celestial gates of Paradise open to admit redeemed mankind.
lit_lat: «Ingressus arcae foederis in portas Sion post victoriam bellicam» (*Super Ps.* 23, n. 7).
spi_lat: «Ascensio Christi in caelum, ubi aperiuntur portae aeternales caeli corpori glorificato et electis» (*ST* III, q. 57, a. 6).

dr_terms: The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: and the Lord shall sit king for ever (*sedebit Dominus rex in aeternum*).
dr_plain: The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: and the Lord shall sit king for ever.
vulgate_text: Dominus diluvium inhabitare facit: et sedebit Dominus rex in aeternum.
locus: Super Ps. 28, n. 10.
lit_eng: YHWH sits enthroned as supreme Sovereign over the primeval chaos and torrential storm floods.
spi_eng: The flood signifies the washing of baptismal regeneration throughout the world, upon which Christ establishes His perpetual spiritual throne in the souls of believers.
lit_lat: «Dominus praesidet aquis diluvii et regnat immobilis super omnes creaturas» (*Super Ps.* 28, n. 10).
spi_lat: «Diluvium est lavacrum Baptismi quo mundatur mundus, in quo Christus sedet rex per gratiam» (*Super Ps.* 28, n. 10).

dr_terms: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness (*virga directionis virga regni tui*). Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity...
dr_plain: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness. Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity...
vulgate_text: Sedes tua Deus in saeculum saeculi: virga directionis virga regni tui. Dilexisti iustitiam, et odisti iniquitatem...
locus: Super Ps. 44, n. 6; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 4; ST III, q. 59, a. 2.
lit_eng: The royal bridegroom addressed as God; in Thomas's exegesis, the literal sense refers prophetically to the Son, whose eternal royal sceptre is spiritual rectitude.
spi_eng: The sceptre of equity is the interior grace of the Holy Spirit ruling the believer's faculties in conformity with divine justice.
lit_lat: «Sedes tua Deus: dicitur ad Filium, ostendens eius divinitatem et aeternitatem regni» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 1, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Virga directionis est iustitia fidei et aequitas Evangelii regens mentes fidelium» (*Super Ps.* 44, n. 6).

dr_terms: For the Lord is high, terrible: a great king over all the earth (*rex magnus super omnem terram*)... For God is the king of all the earth (*rex omnis terrae Deus*): sing ye wisely. God shall reign over the nations (*Regnavit Deus super gentes*): God sitteth on his holy throne.
dr_plain: For the Lord is high, terrible: a great king over all the earth... For God is the king of all the earth: sing ye wisely. God shall reign over the nations: God sitteth on his holy throne.
vulgate_text: Quoniam Dominus excelsus, terribilis; rex magnus super omnem terram... Quoniam rex omnis terrae Deus: psallite sapienter. Regnavit Deus super gentes: Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.
locus: Super Ps. 46, nn. 2, 7–8; ST III, q. 57, a. 1.
lit_eng: Liturgical hymn praising God's universal royal victory over all terrestrial lands.
spi_eng: Prophesies the Ascension of Christ into heaven, where He takes His seat on His celestial throne and extends His gentle spiritual rule over the Gentile Church.
lit_lat: «Laus universalis dominii Dei super omnes gentes» (*Super Ps.* 46, n. 2).
spi_lat: «Ascendit Deus in iubilo: prophetia ascensionis Christi qua regnare coepit super gentes per praedicationem» (*Super Ps.* 46, n. 7).

dr_terms: Give to the king thy judgment, O God: and to the king's son thy justice... And he shall rule from sea to sea (*dominabitur a mari usque ad mare*)... And all kings of the earth shall adore him (*adorabunt eum omnes reges terrae*): all nations shall serve him.
dr_plain: Give to the king thy judgment, O God: and to the king's son thy justice... And he shall rule from sea to sea... And all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him.
vulgate_text: Deus, iudicium tuum regi da: et iustitiam tuam filio regis... Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare... Et adorabunt eum omnes reges terrae: omnes gentes servient ei.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 8. (Super Ps. 71 deest in parte maiori).
lit_eng: Prayer for Solomon, the royal son, that his reign be marked by justice and universal peace.
spi_eng: Solomon typifies Christ the King, to whom the Father commits all judicial authority, commanding all earthly monarchs to submit their temporal rule to His spiritual law.
lit_lat: «Oratio pro pace et iustitia regni Salomonis filii David» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Salomon est figura Christi, cuius dominium extenditur a mari usque ad mare, et cui omnes reges temporales debent subiici» (*De reg.* I, cap. 8).

dr_terms: I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant: Thy seed will I settle for ever. And I will build up thy throne unto generation and generation (*aedificabo in generationem et generationem sedem tuam*)... And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth (*excelsum prae regibus terrae*)... And his throne as the sun before me...
dr_plain: I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant: Thy seed will I settle for ever. And I will build up thy throne unto generation and generation... And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth... And his throne as the sun before me...
vulgate_text: Disposui testamentum electis meis, iuravi David servo meo: Usque in aeternum praeparabo semen tuum. Et aedificabo in generationem et generationem sedem tuam... Et ego primogenitum ponam illum excelsum prae regibus terrae... et thronus eius sicut sol in conspectu meo...
locus: ST III, q. 31, a. 2; ST III, q. 59, a. 2; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 3. (Super Ps. 88 deest).
lit_eng: The irrevocable covenant establishing David's dynasty and seed perpetually in Jerusalem.
spi_eng: Verified strictly in Christ, the Firstborn exalted above all the kings of the earth, whose royal throne endures eternally like the sun.
lit_lat: «Testamentum firmatum David de perpetuitate seminis et throni eius» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Primogenitus excelsus prae regibus terrae est Christus, cuius thronus Ecclesia manet sicut sol in conspectu Dei» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: The Lord hath reigned (*Dominus regnavit*), he is clothed with beauty: the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself... Thy throne is prepared from of old (*Parata sedes tua ex tunc*): thou art from everlasting.
dr_plain: The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself... Thy throne is prepared from of old: thou art from everlasting.
vulgate_text: Dominus regnavit, decorem indutus est: indutus est Dominus fortitudinem, et praecinxit se... Parata sedes tua ex tunc: a saeculo tu es.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 1; In Orat., pet. 2. (Super Ps. 92 deest).
lit_eng: Enthronement psalm declaring the primordial majesty, beauty, and unshakeable antiquity of God's universal reign.
spi_eng: Christ clothed in the beauty of His resurrected body, girded with divine power, establishing His eternal spiritual kingdom over the cosmos.
lit_lat: «Aeterna stabilitas divini regni et providentiae creantis et gubernantis» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Dominus regnavit per carnem assumptam, decorem resurrectionis indutus» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned (*Dominus regnavit*). For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: he will judge the people with justice.
dr_plain: Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned. For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: he will judge the people with justice.
vulgate_text: Dicite in gentibus quia Dominus regnavit. Etenim correxit orbem terrae qui non commovebitur: iudicabit populos in aequitate.
locus: Cat. in Mt., cap. 27; ST III, q. 46, a. 4. (Super Ps. 95 deest).
lit_eng: Summons to proclaim YHWH's righteous governance among all Gentile nations.
spi_eng: The apostolic kerygma announcing that Christ reigns over the world from the wood of the Cross (*regnavit a ligno Deus*), restoring order to a fallen universe.
lit_lat: «Annuntiatio iusti regiminis divini inter omnes populos terrae» (*ST* III, q. 46, a. 4).
spi_lat: «Regnavit a ligno Deus: Christus de cruce regnavit super orbem, corrigens errorem idololatriae» (*Cat. in Mt.*, cap. 27).

dr_terms: The Lord hath reigned (*Dominus regnavit*), let the earth rejoice: let many islands be glad. Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne (*iustitia, et iudicium correctio sedis eius*).
dr_plain: The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: let many islands be glad. Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.
vulgate_text: Dominus regnavit, exsultet terra: laetentur insulae multae. Nubes, et caligo in circuitu eius: iustitia, et iudicium correctio sedis eius.
locus: ST I-II, q. 100, a. 5; In Orat., pet. 2. (Super Ps. 96 deest).
lit_eng: The earth and distant islands rejoice at the manifestation of God's sovereign reign and transcendent holiness.
spi_eng: The interior joy of the believer when the Kingdom of Grace is established within the soul, rooted upon the foundation of divine justice.
lit_lat: «Exsultatio creaturae propter manifestationem iustitiae divinae» (*ST* I-II, q. 100, a. 5).
spi_lat: «Iustitia et iudicium sunt sedes Dei in corde fideli per gratiam inhabitantis» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: The Lord hath reigned (*Dominus regnavit*), let the people tremble: he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved. The Lord is great in Sion, and high above all people.
dr_plain: The Lord hath reigned, let the people tremble: he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved. The Lord is great in Sion, and high above all people.
vulgate_text: Dominus regnavit, irascantur populi: qui sedet super cherubim, moveatur terra. Dominus in Sion magnus: et excelsus super omnes populos.
locus: ST I, q. 108, a. 5; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 4. (Super Ps. 98 deest).
lit_eng: YHWH enthroned upon the Cherubim exercises majestic rule from Mount Zion over all trembling nations.
spi_eng: Christ enthroned above the angelic orders in the heavenly Jerusalem, exercising supreme sapiential governance over all glorified creatures.
lit_lat: «Maiestas Dei regnantis super Cherubim in templo Sion» (*ST* I, q. 108, a. 5).
spi_lat: «Cherubim interpretatur plenitudo scientiae: Deus sedet super mentes contemplativas et angelicas ordines» (*ST* I, q. 108, a. 5).

dr_terms: The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven: and his kingdom shall rule over all (*et regnum ipsius omnibus dominabitur*).
dr_plain: The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven: and his kingdom shall rule over all.
vulgate_text: Dominus in caelo paravit sedem suam: et regnum ipsius omnibus dominabitur.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 1, sed contra; ST I, q. 103, a. 3; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: Primary biblical proof text for universal divine providence: God's throne is celestial, and His kingdom rules universally over all creatures.
spi_eng: The eternal state of glory wherein the elect contemplate God's absolute, unhindered sovereignty without shadow.
lit_lat: «Regnum ipsius omnibus dominabitur: primum argumentum pro universali gubernatione divina» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Thronus in caelo est curia beatorum, ubi voluntas eius perfecte impletur sine ulla rebellione» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: Until I make thy enemies thy footstool. The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion (*Virgam virtutis tuae emittet Dominus ex Sion*): rule thou in the midst of thy enemies (*dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum*).
dr_plain: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: Until I make thy enemies thy footstool. The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.
vulgate_text: Dixit Dominus Domino meo: Sede a dextris meis: Donec ponam inimicos tuos, scabellum pedum tuorum. Virgam virtutis tuae emittet Dominus ex Sion: dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum.
locus: ST III, q. 58, aa. 2–4; ST III, q. 59, a. 1; Super Mt., cap. 22, l. 4; Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 5.
lit_eng: David prophesies that his Lord is seated at YHWH's right hand as eternal Priest and King.
spi_eng: Christ's session at the right hand of the Father denotes equality of divine power, and the supreme judicial and royal authority conferred on His human nature over all enemies.
lit_lat: «Sedere a dextris Patris est aequalitas gloriae in divinitate, et praerogativa iudiciaria in humanitate» (*ST* III, q. 58, a. 3).
spi_lat: «Virga virtutis est Evangelium crucis exiens ex Sion ad subiiciendum mundum Christo» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 22, l. 4).

dr_terms: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom (*Gloriam regni tui dicent*): and shall tell of thy power... Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages (*Regnum tuum regnum omnium saeculorum*): and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.
dr_plain: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom: and shall tell of thy power... Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages: and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.
vulgate_text: Gloriam regni tui dicent: et potentiam tuam loquentur... Regnum tuum regnum omnium saeculorum: et dominatio tua in omni generatione et generationem.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 2; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: The saints praise the perpetual, unshakeable duration of God's universal royal dominion across all ages.
spi_eng: The beatific contemplation in the Church Triumphant, where the glorified saints endlessly proclaim the unveiled splendor of God's kingdom.
lit_lat: «Laus aeternitatis et magnificentiae regni Dei ab omnibus sanctis» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Sancti in patria gloriam regni eius facie ad faciem contemplantur et narrant» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: The Lord shall reign for ever (*Regnabit Dominus in saecula*): thy God, O Sion, unto generation and generation.
dr_plain: The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, unto generation and generation.
vulgate_text: Regnabit Dominus in saecula, Deus tuus Sion: in generationem et generationem.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2. (Super Ps. 145 deest).
lit_eng: The Lord God of Zion reigns perpetually over His holy city from generation to generation.
spi_eng: The eternal reign of Christ in the heavenly Jerusalem, where the communion of saints is confirmed in everlasting peace.
lit_lat: «Perpetua regalis protectio Dei super civitatem Sion» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Christus Deus tuus regnabit in Sion caelesti, idest in Ecclesia triumphantium in aeternum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: By me kings reign (*Per me reges regnant*), and lawgivers decree just things, by me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice.
dr_plain: By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things, by me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice.
vulgate_text: Per me reges regnant, et legum conditores iusta decernunt; per me principes imperant, et potentes decernunt iustitiam.
locus: ST I-II, q. 93, a. 3; De reg. I, cap. 1; Sent. II, d. 44, q. 1, a. 2.
lit_eng: Divine Wisdom is the foundation of all civil authority, so that temporal monarchs rule justly only by participating in Eternal Law.
spi_eng: The infused gift of Wisdom enables the believer to govern his own soul, exercising true moral kingship over his internal appetites.
lit_lat: «Lex aeterna est ipsa divina sapientia secundum quam omnis potestas terrena legitime iudicat» (*ST* I-II, q. 93, a. 3).
spi_lat: «Sapiens regit seipsum et motus suos per participationem divinae sapientiae» (*Sent.* II, d. 44, q. 1, a. 2).

dr_terms: They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever (*regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum*).
dr_plain: They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
vulgate_text: Iudicabunt nationes et dominabuntur populis, et regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum.
locus: ST Suppl., q. 89, a. 1; ST III, q. 59, a. 5.
lit_eng: The vindication and reward of the righteous after mortal trials, reigning perpetually with God.
spi_eng: The glorified saints participate in Christ's judicial and royal authority, sitting as assessors with Him at the Last Judgment.
lit_lat: «Exaltatio iustorum post persecutiones temporales» (*ST* Suppl., q. 89, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Sancti iudicabunt et regnabunt cum Christo ut assessores iudicis in die iudicii et in gloria» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 5).

dr_terms: Therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to the everlasting kingdom (*ad regnum perpetuum*). If then your delight be in thrones, and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, love wisdom, that you may reign for ever (*ut in perpetuum regnetis*).
dr_plain: Therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to the everlasting kingdom. If then your delight be in thrones, and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, love wisdom, that you may reign for ever.
vulgate_text: Concupiscentia itaque sapientiae deducet ad regnum perpetuum. Si ergo delectamini sedibus, et sceptris, o reges populi, diligite sapientiam, ut in perpetuum regnetis.
locus: De reg. I, cap. 9; ST II-II, q. 45, a. 1.
lit_eng: Admonition to secular rulers that the pursuit of divine wisdom is the only path to an enduring, incorruptible kingdom.
spi_eng: Worldly monarchs must direct their temporal authority toward supernatural beatitude, wherein alone true and eternal royalty is found.
lit_lat: «Monitio regibus terrae ut sapientiam divinam quaerant ad regnum obtinendum» (*De reg.* I, cap. 9).
spi_lat: «Verum et perpetuum regnum non est temporale sed beatitudo aeterna qua anima fruitur Deo» (*De reg.* I, cap. 9).

dr_terms: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God (*ostendit illi regnum Dei*), and gave him the knowledge of the holy things...
dr_plain: She conducted the just, when he fled from his brother's wrath, through the right ways, and shewed him the kingdom of God, and gave him the knowledge of the holy things...
vulgate_text: Iustum autem perfugam a fratris ira deduxit per vias rectas, et ostendit illi regnum Dei, et dedit illi scientiam sanctorum...
locus: ST II-II, q. 180, a. 3, ad 4; Super Io., cap. 1, l. 16.
lit_eng: Wisdom guides Jacob fleeing from Esau and grants him the visionary ladder at Bethel (*regnum Dei*).
spi_eng: Jacob's ladder typifies the contemplative ascent of the soul to spiritual union with God and intuitive knowledge of celestial mysteries.
lit_lat: «Sapientia ostendit Iacob fugienti scalam caeli et angelos ascendentes et descendentes» (*ST* II-II, q. 180, a. 3, ad 4).
spi_lat: «Ostendit illi regnum Dei, idest contemplationem divinorum per gratiam viatoribus concessam» (*Super Io.*, cap. 1, l. 16).

dr_terms: All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the most High (*testamentum Altissimi*), and the knowledge of truth.
dr_plain: All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the most High, and the knowledge of truth.
vulgate_text: Haec omnia liber vitae, et testamentum Altissimi, et agnitio veritatis.
locus: ST I-II, q. 106, a. 1; Super Ps. prol.
lit_eng: Divine Wisdom is identified with the historical book of the Mosaic covenant given to the congregation of Jacob.
spi_eng: Prefigures the New Law of the Gospel, which is the internal law of the Kingdom of God written by the Holy Spirit in human hearts.
lit_lat: «Lex scripta Moysi continens mandata Dei data populo Iudaeorum» (*ST* I-II, q. 106, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Praefiguratio Legis Novae, quae est lex indita Spiritus Sancti et ipsum regnum Dei in nobis» (*ST* I-II, q. 106, a. 1).

dr_terms: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: and he gave him a covenant of the kingdom (*testamentum regni*), and a throne of glory (*sedem gloriae*) in Israel.
dr_plain: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: and he gave him a covenant of the kingdom, and a throne of glory in Israel.
vulgate_text: Dominus abstulit peccata ipsius, et exaltavit in aeternum cornu eius: et dedit illi testamentum regni, et sedem gloriae in Israel.
locus: ST III, q. 31, a. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Sirach).
lit_eng: Eulogy of David: God forgave his transgression and granted him an everlasting covenant of the kingdom in Israel.
spi_eng: The 'covenant of the kingdom' finds its definitive reality in the spiritual, incorruptible throne of Jesus Christ.
lit_lat: «Testamentum regni datum David propter misericordiam et poenitentiam eius» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Sedes gloriae Davidis spiritualiter impletur in Christo, cuius regni non erit finis» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).

dr_terms: I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated (*sedentem super solium excelsum et elevatum*)... and my eyes have seen the King the Lord of hosts (*regem Dominum exercituum*).
dr_plain: I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated... and my eyes have seen the King the Lord of hosts.
vulgate_text: Vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum et elevatum... et regem Dominum exercituum vidi oculis meis.
locus: Super Is., cap. 6; Super Io., cap. 12, l. 7; ST I, q. 12, a. 11.
lit_eng: Isaiah beholds a majestic theophany of YHWH the King enthroned in the celestial sanctuary.
spi_eng: John 12:41 identifies this vision as the pre-incarnate glory of Christ, revealing the eternal kingship of the Son.
lit_lat: «Isaias vidit Deum sub specie regis sedentis in maiestate sua in templo» (*Super Is.*, cap. 6).
spi_lat: «Haec dixit Isaias quando vidit gloriam eius, scilicet Christi, et locutus est de eo» (*Super Io.*, cap. 12, l. 7).

dr_terms: For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder (*factus est principatus super humerum eius*)... he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom (*super solium David, et super regnum eius*); to establish it and strengthen it with judgment and with justice, from henceforth and for ever.
dr_plain: For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder... he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom; to establish it and strengthen it with judgment and with justice, from henceforth and for ever.
vulgate_text: Parvulus enim natus est nobis, et filius datus est nobis, et factus est principatus super humerum eius... super solium David, et super regnum eius sedebit, ut confirmet illud et corroboret in iudicio et iustitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum.
locus: Super Is., cap. 9; ST III, q. 35, a. 7; Super Mt., cap. 1, l. 1.
lit_eng: Prophecy of the birth of the divine child who inherits David's throne and establishes an everlasting government of peace.
spi_eng: 'Government upon His shoulder' is the Cross, by which Christ conquers demonic tyranny and establishes the interior peace of grace in the soul.
lit_lat: «Principatus super humerum eius: clavis domus David, idest potestas regia collata Christo nato» (*Super Is.*, cap. 9).
spi_lat: «Principatus super humerum est crux quam ipsemet baiulavit, per quam regnum acquisivit et pacem» (*Super Is.*, cap. 9).

dr_terms: And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse... But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth (*virga oris sui*)...
dr_plain: And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse... But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth...
vulgate_text: Et egredietur virga de radice Iesse... sed iudicabit in iustitia pauperes, et arguet in aequitate pro mansuetis terrae: et percutiet terram virga oris sui...
locus: Super Is., cap. 11; ST I-II, q. 68, a. 1; ST III, q. 7, a. 1.
lit_eng: The Davidic Branch anointed with the sevenfold Spirit to judge the poor with divine equity.
spi_eng: The seven Gifts of the Holy Spirit governing the interior powers of the soul, ruling the believer through the spiritual word of Christ's mouth.
lit_lat: «Virga de radice Iesse est Christus, iudicans pauperes in iustitia per donum consilii et iudicii» (*Super Is.*, cap. 11).
spi_lat: «Virga oris eius est verbum Evangelii et septem dona Spiritus Sancti regnantia in corde iusti» (*ST* I-II, q. 68, a. 1).

dr_terms: And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Sion (*cum regnaverit Dominus exercituum in monte Sion*), and in Jerusalem, and shall be glorified in the sight of his ancients.
dr_plain: And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem, and shall be glorified in the sight of his ancients.
vulgate_text: Et erubescet luna, et confundetur sol, cum regnaverit Dominus exercituum in monte Sion, et in Ierusalem, et in conspectu senum suorum fuerit glorificatus.
locus: Super Is., cap. 24; ST Suppl., q. 91, a. 2.
lit_eng: Cosmic apocalyptic judgment where created luminaries are confounded before the manifest glory of YHWH's reign in Jerusalem.
spi_eng: The final glory of the New Jerusalem where created sun and moon yield to the uncreated splendor of God, who illumines the blessed forever.
lit_lat: «Confusio luminarium terrae prae fulgore praesentiae Dei iudicantis in Sion» (*Super Is.*, cap. 24).
spi_lat: «In regno caelesti claritas corporum caelestium superabitur a claritate Dei et beatorum» (*ST* Suppl., q. 91, a. 2).

dr_terms: Behold a king shall reign in justice (*in iustitia regnabit rex*), and princes shall rule in judgment.
dr_plain: Behold a king shall reign in justice, and princes shall rule in judgment.
vulgate_text: Ecce in iustitia regnabit rex, et principes in iudicio praeerunt.
locus: Super Is., cap. 32; Super Mt., cap. 19, l. 3.
lit_eng: Prophecy of a righteous monarch governing with just ministers.
spi_eng: The King is Christ; the princes ruling under Him are the Apostles and their episcopal successors who govern the Church Militant in spiritual equity.
lit_lat: «Rex iustus est Ezechias contra Sennacherib, et principes eius duces fideles» (*Super Is.*, cap. 32).
spi_lat: «Litteraliter spiritualiter: Rex est Christus regnans in iustitia; principes sunt Apostoli et praelati iudicantes in Ecclesia» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 19, l. 3).

dr_terms: For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king (*Dominus rex noster*): he will save us.
dr_plain: For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king: he will save us.
vulgate_text: Dominus enim iudex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster: ipse salvabit nos.
locus: Super Is., cap. 33; ST I-II, q. 100, a. 8; ST III, q. 59, a. 1.
lit_eng: The people of Zion profess that YHWH unites in Himself all sovereign judicial, legislative, and executive authority.
spi_eng: Thomas proves that the threefold powers of sovereign government subsist preeminently in Christ as Savior and King of His Church.
lit_lat: «In Deo solo concurrunt perfecte tria: iudicium, legislatio et regia defensio populi sui» (*Super Is.*, cap. 33).
spi_lat: «Christus est noster legifer per Evangelium, iudex in conscientia et iudicio, et rex nos salvans per sanguinem suum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).

dr_terms: Say to the cities of Juda: Behold your God: Behold the Lord God shall come with strength, and his arm shall rule (*brachium eius dominabitur*)...
dr_plain: Say to the cities of Juda: Behold your God: Behold the Lord God shall come with strength, and his arm shall rule...
vulgate_text: Dic civitatibus Iuda: Ecce Deus vester: Ecce Dominus Deus in virtute veniet, et brachium eius dominabitur...
locus: Super Is., cap. 40; Super Mt., cap. 3, l. 1.
lit_eng: The herald proclaims the arrival of the sovereign Lord coming in strength to shepherd and rule Judah.
spi_eng: The 'arm of the Lord' is the Incarnate Son, through whom the Father accomplishes redemption and establishes His royal reign among men.
lit_lat: «Annuntiatio liberationis de Babylone per virtutem divinam» (*Super Is.*, cap. 40).
spi_lat: «Brachium eius est Christus Filius Dei, per quem Deus operatus est salutem et regnum suum manifestavit» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 3, l. 1).

dr_terms: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings... that saith to Sion: Thy God shall reign! (*Regnavit Deus tuus!*)
dr_plain: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings... that saith to Sion: Thy God shall reign!
vulgate_text: Quam pulchri super montes pedes annunciantis... praedicantis salutem: dicentis Sion: Regnavit Deus tuus!
locus: Super Is., cap. 52; Super Rom., cap. 10, l. 2; Super Mt., cap. 4, l. 2.
lit_eng: The messenger announces the end of Babylonian exile and the return of YHWH's kingship to Zion.
spi_eng: The preaching of the Apostles announcing the liberation of mankind from the captivity of sin and the inauguration of the Kingdom of Grace.
lit_lat: «Nuntius veniens trans montes annuntians liberationem Ierusalem: regnavit Deus tuus» (*Super Is.*, cap. 52).
spi_lat: «Pedes evangelizantium sunt Apostoli annuntiantes regnum gratiae Christi per universum mundum» (*Super Rom.*, cap. 10, l. 2).

dr_terms: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign (*regnabit rex*), and shall be wise: and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
dr_plain: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will raise up to David a just branch: and a king shall reign, and shall be wise: and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
vulgate_text: Ecce dies veniunt, ait Dominus, et suscitabo David germen iustum: et regnabit rex, et sapiens erit: et faciet iudicium et iustitiam in terra.
locus: Super Ier., cap. 23; ST III, q. 31, a. 2.
lit_eng: Prophecy of the righteous Branch of David reigning as a wise King executing justice in Judah.
spi_eng: Christ the King imparts His own justice to the soul through faith, justifying the sinner and establishing interior peace.
lit_lat: «Prophetia de Christo nato de semine David, qui regnabit vere et iudicium faciet» (*Super Ier.*, cap. 23).
spi_lat: «Hoc est nomen quod vocabunt eum: Dominus iustus noster, quia per eius regnum iustificamur gratis» (*ST* III, q. 31, a. 2).

dr_terms: There shall not be cut off from David a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel (*qui sedeat super thronum domus Israel*).
dr_plain: There shall not be cut off from David a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel.
vulgate_text: Non interibit de David vir qui sedeat super thronum domus Israel.
locus: Super Ier., cap. 33; ST III, q. 22, a. 1.
lit_eng: God's covenant promising perpetual continuity to David's royal throne and the Levitical priesthood.
spi_eng: The perpetual kingship and priesthood find their indivisible, eternal fulfillment in Christ, the high Priest and King of the spiritual Israel.
lit_lat: «Promissio perpetuitatis seminis Davidici et sacerdotii Levitici» (*Super Ier.*, cap. 33).
spi_lat: «Utrumque impletur in Christo, qui est simul rex aeternus in throno et sacerdos in aeternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech» (*ST* III, q. 22, a. 1).

dr_terms: And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David... and my servant David the prince in the midst of them (*servus meus David princeps in medio eorum*): I the Lord have spoken it.
dr_plain: And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David... and my servant David the prince in the midst of them: I the Lord have spoken it.
vulgate_text: Et suscitabo super eas pastorem unum qui pascat eas, servum meum David... et servus meus David princeps in medio eorum: ego Dominus locutus sum.
locus: Super Io., cap. 10, l. 3. (Super Ezech. deest).
lit_eng: God promises to deliver His flock from negligent hirelings by appointing His servant David as sole shepherd and prince.
spi_eng: Fulfilled in Christ the Good Shepherd and King, who feeds His Church with His own Body and Blood in the Eucharist.
lit_lat: «Promissio unius pastoris et principis liberantis gregem a malis pastoribus» (*Super Io.*, cap. 10, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Servus meus David est Christus, princeps et pastor bonus pascens Ecclesiam proprio corpore et sanguine» (*Super Io.*, cap. 10, l. 3).

dr_terms: And my servant David shall be king over them (*servus meus David rex super eos*), and they shall have one shepherd... and David my servant shall be their prince for ever (*princeps eorum in perpetuum*).
dr_plain: And my servant David shall be king over them, and they shall have one shepherd... and David my servant shall be their prince for ever.
vulgate_text: Et servus meus David rex super eos, et pastor unus erit omnium eorum... et David servus meus princeps eorum in perpetuum.
locus: ST III, q. 8, a. 1. (Super Ezech. deest).
lit_eng: Prophetic reunification of Judah and Ephraim into a single undivided nation under one Davidic king forever.
spi_eng: The universal unity of the Catholic Church, wherein Jews and Gentiles are united as one flock under Christ the Head.
lit_lat: «Reunio duarum tribuum sub uno principe Davidico perpetuo» (*ST* III, q. 8, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Unitas Ecclesiae catholicae ex Iudaeis et gentibus congregata sub uno capite et rege Christo» (*ST* III, q. 8, a. 1).

dr_terms: But in the days of those kingdoms the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed (*suscitabit Deus caeli regnum, quod in aeternum non dissipabitur*), and his kingdom shall not be delivered up to another people (*regnum eius alteri populo non tradetur*), and it shall break in pieces, and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.
dr_plain: But in the days of those kingdoms the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, and his kingdom shall not be delivered up to another people, and it shall break in pieces, and shall consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand for ever.
vulgate_text: In diebus autem regnorum illorum suscitabit Deus caeli regnum, quod in aeternum non dissipabitur, et regnum eius alteri populo non tradetur: comminuet autem, et consumet universa regna haec, et ipsum stabit in aeternum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 21, l. 4; ST III, q. 59, a. 2; De reg. I, cap. 14.
lit_eng: Daniel interprets the stone cut without hands shattering the metallic statue as an unshakeable kingdom established by God during the fourth empire.
spi_eng: The Stone is Christ born of a Virgin, who during the Roman Empire founded a spiritual kingdom that subdues earthly empires and stands for all eternity.
lit_lat: «Lapis abscissus sine manibus est Christus natus de Virgine, destruens regna terrena et erigens regnum sempiternum» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 21, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Regnum Christi alteri populo non tradetur, quia Ecclesia manet usque ad finem saeculi et transfertur in gloriam» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom (*Regnum eius regnum sempiternum*), and his power to all generations... for his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is to all generations (*regnum eius in generationem et generationem*).
dr_plain: His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his power to all generations... for his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is to all generations.
vulgate_text: Regnum eius regnum sempiternum, et potestas eius in generationem et generationem... quia potestas eius sempiterna est, et regnum eius in generationem et generationem.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 8.
lit_eng: Nebuchadnezzar's public decree acknowledging the everlasting, unshakeable sovereignty of the God of heaven after his humiliation.
spi_eng: The proud intellect of man, humbled by divine discipline, subdues its own vanity to confess the absolute sovereignty of God's grace.
lit_lat: «Professio Nabuchodonosor recognoscentis solum Deum habere potestatem sempiternam» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Humiliatio superbiae humanae confitentis divinum dominium super omnes potestates saeculi» (*De reg.* I, cap. 8).

dr_terms: I beheld therefore in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the son of man came with the clouds of heaven... And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom (*dedit ei potestatem, et honorem, et regnum*): and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him: his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed (*regnum eius, quod non corrumpetur*).
dr_plain: I beheld therefore in the vision of the night, and lo, one like the son of man came with the clouds of heaven... And he gave him power, and glory, and a kingdom: and all peoples, tribes and tongues shall serve him: his power is an everlasting power that shall not be taken away: and his kingdom that shall not be destroyed.
vulgate_text: Aspiciebam ergo in visione noctis, et ecce cum nubibus caeli quasi filius hominis veniebat... Et dedit ei potestatem, et honorem, et regnum: et omnes populi, tribus, et linguae servient ei: potestas eius, potestas aeterna, quae non auferetur: et regnum eius, quod non corrumpetur.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 1, sed contra; ST III, q. 59, a. 3; Super Mt., cap. 26, l. 6; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: Vision of the Son of Man presented before the Ancient of Days, receiving universal and incorruptible kingship.
spi_eng: Thomas's decisive proof text: Christ receives universal judicial power and royal dominion from the Father specifically in His human nature as the Son of Man.
lit_lat: «Filius hominis accipit regnum et potestatem iudiciariam a Patre secundum humanam naturam» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Regnum eius non corrumpetur: potestas Christi iudiciaria consummabitur in die novissimo quando omnia ei plene subicientur» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: But the saints of the most high God shall take the kingdom (*suscipient regnum sancti Dei altissimi*): and they shall possess the kingdom for ever and ever... And that the kingdom, and power, and the greatness of the kingdom (*regnum, et potestas, et magnitudo regni*), under all the heaven, may be given to the people of the saints of the most High: whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom (*cuius regnum sempiternum est regnum*), and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.
dr_plain: But the saints of the most high God shall take the kingdom: and they shall possess the kingdom for ever and ever... And that the kingdom, and power, and the greatness of the kingdom, under all the heaven, may be given to the people of the saints of the most High: whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve him, and shall obey him.
vulgate_text: Et suscipient regnum sancti Dei altissimi, et obtinebunt regnum usque in saeculum, et in saeculum saeculorum... Et regnum, et potestas, et magnitudo regni, quae est subter omne caelum, detur populo sanctorum Altissimi: cuius regnum sempiternum est regnum, et omnes reges servient ei, et obedient.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 5; Super I Cor., cap. 6, l. 1.
lit_eng: The apocalyptic promise that the holy people of God will ultimately receive the universal dominion formerly held by oppressive beasts.
spi_eng: The elect receive the kingdom by union with Christ, sharing initially in His royal authority on earth and consummately on thrones of glory in heaven.
lit_lat: «Populus sanctorum accipiet dominatum post destructionem bestiarum tyrannicarum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 5).
spi_lat: «Sancti accipiunt regnum per unionem ad Christum: in praesenti per fidem et gratiam, in futuro per beatitudinem et consessum iudiciarium» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 6, l. 1).

dr_terms: And saviours shall come up into mount Sion to judge the mount of Esau: and the kingdom shall be for the Lord (*erit Domino regnum*).
dr_plain: And saviours shall come up into mount Sion to judge the mount of Esau: and the kingdom shall be for the Lord.
vulgate_text: Et ascendent salvatores in montem Sion iudicare montem Esau: et erit Domino regnum.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Abdiam).
lit_eng: Prophecy of deliverers ascending Mount Zion to exercise judgment over Edom, establishing YHWH's undisputed rule.
spi_eng: The final public triumph of Christ and His saints over the worldly and demonic powers at the end of the world.
lit_lat: «Salvatores ascendentes in montem Sion ad iudicandum gentem Idumaeorum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Erit Domino regnum: consummatio regni quando omnes inimici et daemones plene subiicientur Christo» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: And the Lord will reign over them in mount Sion (*regnabit Dominus super eos in monte Sion*), from this time now and for ever. And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock... the former power shall come, the kingdom to the daughter of Jerusalem (*regnum filiae Ierusalem*).
dr_plain: And the Lord will reign over them in mount Sion, from this time now and for ever. And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock... the former power shall come, the kingdom to the daughter of Jerusalem.
vulgate_text: Et regnabit Dominus super eos in monte Sion ex hoc nunc et usque in aeternum. Et tu turris gregis nebulosa... veniet potestas prima, regnum filiae Ierusalem.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Michaeam).
lit_eng: YHWH's perpetual reign over the restored remnant in Mount Zion, returning the primordial royal dominion to Jerusalem.
spi_eng: The restoration of spiritual royalty to the Church, the true daughter of Jerusalem, which inherits Christ's incorruptible kingdom.
lit_lat: «Restauratio dominii pristini Davidici in monte Sion post captivitatem» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Filia Ierusalem est Ecclesia, cui redditur potestas prima per adoptionem filiorum Dei» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: And thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel (*qui sit dominator in Israel*): and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.
dr_plain: And thou, Bethlehem Ephrata, art a little one among the thousands of Juda: out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be the ruler in Israel: and his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity.
vulgate_text: Et tu Bethlehem Ephrata parvulus es in millibus Iuda: ex te mihi egredietur qui sit dominator in Israel, et egressus eius ab initio, a diebus aeternitatis.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 2, l. 2; ST III, q. 35, a. 7.
lit_eng: Prophecy of the birthplace of the Davidic Ruler whose origin is from eternity.
spi_eng: Asserts both the eternal generation of Christ the King ('from the days of eternity') and His temporal human birth in Bethlehem.
lit_lat: «Dominator in Israel egredietur ex Bethlehem, natus temporaliter secundum carnem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 2, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Egressus eius a diebus aeternitatis: duplex generatio Christi, scilicet aeterna ex Patre, et temporalis ex Virgine» (*ST* III, q. 35, a. 7).

dr_terms: The king of Israel the Lord (*Rex Israel Dominus*) is in the midst of thee, thou shalt fear evil no more.
dr_plain: The king of Israel the Lord is in the midst of thee, thou shalt fear evil no more.
vulgate_text: Rex Israel Dominus in medio tui, non timebis malum ultra.
locus: Cat. in Io., cap. 1; ST III, q. 37, a. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Sophoniam).
lit_eng: The presence of YHWH as King dwelling in the midst of Jerusalem removes all dread of temporal enemies.
spi_eng: The indwelling presence of the Incarnate King in the soul through sanctifying grace expels the terror of sin and death.
lit_lat: «Liberatio Ierusalem a timore hostili propter praesentiam regis Domini in medio eius» (*ST* III, q. 37, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Rex Israel Christus inhabitat per gratiam animam fidelem, auferens omnem timorem servilem et damnationis» (*Cat. in Io.*, cap. 1).

dr_terms: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem: BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee (*ECCE REX TUUS veniet tibi*), the just and saviour: he is poor, and riding upon an ass... and he shall rule from sea to sea (*dominabitur a mari usque ad mare*)...
dr_plain: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion, shout for joy, O daughter of Jerusalem: BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee, the just and saviour: he is poor, and riding upon an ass... and he shall rule from sea to sea...
vulgate_text: Exsulta satis filia Sion, iubila filia Ierusalem: ECCE REX TUUS veniet tibi iustus, et salvator: ipse pauper, et ascendens super asinam... et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 21, l. 1; ST III, q. 59, a. 4; De reg. I, cap. 1.
lit_eng: The messianic King entering Jerusalem in humility riding upon an ass, extending peace to all nations.
spi_eng: Christ enters the human soul through meekness, proving that His kingship seeks not earthly pomp, but the interior salvation of hearts.
lit_lat: «Ingressus regis humilis sedentis super asinam in Ierusalem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 21, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Rex tuus venit pauper, non cum pompa saeculari aut armis militaribus, sed ut spiritualiter salvet mentes mansuetudine sua» (*De reg.* I, cap. 1).

dr_terms: And the Lord shall be king over all the earth (*erit Dominus rex super omnem terram*): in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name shall be one.
dr_plain: And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day there shall be one Lord, and his name shall be one.
vulgate_text: Et erit Dominus rex super omnem terram: in die illa erit Dominus unus, et erit nomen eius unum.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 3; In Orat., pet. 2. (Nullus commentarius directus in Zachariam).
lit_eng: Eschatological prophecy that YHWH alone will be acknowledged as King over all the earth.
spi_eng: The definitive eradication of all idolatry and error, when God's sole reign is confessed universally by all the elect at the Parousia.
lit_lat: «Cessatio omnis idololatriae et unius Dei cultus per universam terram» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 3).
spi_lat: «Consummatio regni quando omnes electi in una fide et caritate subicientur uni Domino sine discordia» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: For I am a great King (*rex magnus ego sum*), saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles.
dr_plain: For I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles.
vulgate_text: Quia rex magnus ego sum, dicit Dominus exercituum, et nomen meum horribile in gentibus.
locus: ST III, q. 73, a. 4; ST III, q. 83, a. 1. (Nullus commentarius directus in Malachiam).
lit_eng: YHWH rebukes unworthy Levitical temple sacrifices by asserting that He is a great King revered among the Gentiles.
spi_eng: Prophesies the cessation of carnal sacrifices and the institution of the clean Eucharistic oblation offered in the Church across all nations.
lit_lat: «Deus reprobat sacrificia immunda Iudaeorum, asserens suam regalem maiestatem inter gentes» (*ST* III, q. 73, a. 4).
spi_lat: «Praedictio sacrificii Novi Testamenti, scilicet Eucharistiae, quae offertur magno Regi in omni loco a gentibus» (*ST* III, q. 83, a. 1).

dr_terms: Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven (*regnum caelorum*) is at hand.
dr_plain: Do penance: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
vulgate_text: Poenitentiam agite: appropinquavit enim regnum caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 3, l. 1.
lit_eng: John the Baptist proclaims that the long-awaited Messianic era has arrived in the person of Christ.
spi_eng: Thomas outlines: (1) Christ Himself (*Autobasileia*), (2) Sacred Scripture / doctrine, (3) Church Militant, (4) Justice of faith in the soul (tropological), (5) Heavenly glory of the Church Triumphant (anagogical).
lit_lat: «De adventu Christi in carnem, qui est initium regni Novi Testamenti» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 3, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Regnum caelorum dicitur multipliciter: primo Christus ipse; secundo Sacra Scriptura; tertio Ecclesia militans; quarto iustitia fidei; quinto curia caelestis» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 3, l. 1).

dr_terms: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven (*regnum caelorum*) is at hand... preaching the gospel of the kingdom (*evangelium regni*): and healing all manner of sickness...
dr_plain: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say: Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand... preaching the gospel of the kingdom: and healing all manner of sickness...
vulgate_text: Exinde coepit Iesus praedicare, et dicere: Poenitentiam agite: appropinquavit enim regnum caelorum... praedicans evangelium regni, et sanans omnem languorem...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 4, l. 2.
lit_eng: Christ opens His public ministry, authenticating the Gospel of the Kingdom by miracles of physical healing.
spi_eng: The healing of bodily diseases signifies the spiritual cure of vices wrought interiorly by the grace of the Gospel.
lit_lat: «Christus incipit praedicare doctrinam Evangelii et sanare languores ad confirmationem regni» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 4, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Evangelium regni promittit non bona terrena sicut vetus lex, sed caelestia et spiritualia» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 4, l. 2).

dr_terms: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven (*regnum caelorum*)... Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven (*regnum caelorum*).
dr_plain: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven... Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
vulgate_text: Beati pauperes spiritu: quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum... Beati qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam: quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 5, l. 1; ST I-II, q. 69, a. 2.
lit_eng: The Beatitudes: Christ promises the Kingdom of Heaven to the humble and to those who endure persecution for justice.
spi_eng: Promised in the present tense (*est*) because humility already possesses the initial seed of the Kingdom through grace, which blossoms into celestial beatitude.
lit_lat: «Promissio regni caelorum pauperibus spiritu et persecutionem patientibus» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 5, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Dicitur in praesenti 'ipsorum est', quia per humilitatem et caritatem iusti iam possident inchoationem beatitudinis per spem et gratiam» (*ST* I-II, q. 69, a. 2).

dr_terms: He therefore that shall break one of these least commandments... shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven (*in regno caelorum*)... unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven (*non intrabitis in regnum caelorum*).
dr_plain: He therefore that shall break one of these least commandments... shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven... unless your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
vulgate_text: Qui ergo solverit unum de mandatis istis minimis... minimus vocabitur in regno caelorum... nisi abundaverit iustitia vestra plus quam scribarum, et pharisaeorum, non intrabitis in regnum caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 5, l. 2; ST I-II, q. 107, a. 1.
lit_eng: The perfection of the New Law requires internal observance of the heart surpassing the externalism of the Pharisees.
spi_eng: 'Kingdom of heaven' denotes either the Church Militant (where an unfaithful teacher is esteemed least) or the Church Triumphant (entered only by those possessing infused justice).
lit_lat: «Doctrina moralis Novi Testamenti perficiens veterem legem quoad mandata interiora» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 5, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Regnum caelorum hic accipitur dupliciter: vel pro Ecclesia praesenti, in qua minimus est qui docet et non facit; vel pro vita beata, in quam non intrant nisi abundantes iustitia caritatis» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 5, l. 2).

dr_terms: Thy kingdom come (*Adveniat regnum tuum*). Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven... Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God (*primum regnum Dei*), and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you.
dr_plain: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven... Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you.
vulgate_text: Adveniat regnum tuum. Fiat voluntas tua, sicut in caelo et in terra... Quaerite ergo primum regnum Dei, et iustitiam eius: et haec omnia adiicientur vobis.
locus: In Orat., pet. 2; Super Mt., cap. 6, ll. 2, 6; ST II-II, q. 83, a. 9.
lit_eng: The Lord's Prayer: petitioning the establishment of God's sovereign will and prioritizing the Kingdom above temporal goods.
spi_eng: Thomas distinguishes: (1) Manifestation of Christ's universal dominion over all creatures (eschatological), (2) The glory of Paradise (anagogical), (3) God reigning in the soul through grace rather than sin (tropological).
lit_lat: «Oratio ut voluntas Dei fiat in nobis sicut in angelis et ut regnum eius percipiamus» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 6, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Tripliciter: primo quantum ad manifestandam potestatem divinam in omnes; secundo regnum dicitur gloria Paradisi; tertio ut non regnet peccatum in nobis, sed Deus per gratiam» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven (*intrabit in regnum caelorum*): but he that doth the will of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven (*intrabit in regnum caelorum*).
dr_plain: Not every one that saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven: but he that doth the will of my Father who is in heaven, he shall enter into the kingdom of heaven.
vulgate_text: Non omnis qui dicit mihi, Domine, Domine, intrabit in regnum caelorum: sed qui facit voluntatem Patris mei, qui in caelis est, ipse intrabit in regnum caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 7, l. 3; ST II-II, q. 4, a. 5.
lit_eng: Verbal confession of Christ without moral obedience to the Father does not admit a man into the Kingdom of Heaven.
spi_eng: Formless faith (*fides informis*) is insufficient for salvation; entrance into beatitude requires faith animated by charity (*fides formata*) and meritorious works.
lit_lat: «Non sufficit confessio oris sine operibus iustitiae ad introitum regni» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 7, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Fides informis non sufficit ad salutem, sed requiritur fides formata caritate, quae facit voluntatem Patris» (*ST* II-II, q. 4, a. 5).

dr_terms: And I say to you that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven (*in regno caelorum*): But the children of the kingdom (*filii autem regni*) shall be cast out into the exterior darkness...
dr_plain: And I say to you that many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into the exterior darkness...
vulgate_text: Dico autem vobis quod multi ab oriente, et occidente venient, et recumbent cum Abraham, et Isaac, et Iacob in regno caelorum: filii autem regni eiicientur in tenebras exteriores...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 8, l. 2; ST II-II, q. 10, a. 1.
lit_eng: Gentiles will enter the heavenly banquet of the patriarchs through faith, while unbelieving children of the covenant are excluded.
spi_eng: The historical Jews who possessed the type and promise of the kingdom are cast out for rejecting Christ, while Gentiles enter the reality of the Church and glory.
lit_lat: «Vocatio gentium ad fidem Abrahae et reprobatio Iudaeorum incredulorum» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 8, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Filii regni carnales eiiciuntur propter infidelitatem, et gentiles recumbunt in convivio aeternae beatitudinis per fidem spiritualem» (*ST* II-II, q. 10, a. 1).

dr_terms: Amen I say to you, there hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist: yet he that is the lesser in the kingdom of heaven (*in regno caelorum*) is greater than he. And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence (*regnum caelorum vim patitur*), and the violent bear it away.
dr_plain: Amen I say to you, there hath not risen among them that are born of women a greater than John the Baptist: yet he that is the lesser in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. And from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away.
vulgate_text: Amen dico vobis, non surrexit inter natos mulierum maior Ioanne Baptista: qui autem minor est in regno caelorum, maior est illo. A diebus autem Ioannis Baptistae usque nunc, regnum caelorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 11, l. 2; ST I-II, q. 106, a. 4; ST III, q. 38, a. 1.
lit_eng: John the Baptist marks the boundary of the Old Law; the New Covenant offers superior dignity.
spi_eng: 'He that is lesser' refers literally to Christ (who was younger and deemed inferior by men) or anagogically to the least glorified saint in heaven, who surpasses any mortal prophet.
lit_lat: «Ioannes est terminus veteris testamenti et aurora novi» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 11, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Minor in regno: vel ipse Christus, qui tempore et aestimatione hominum minor fuit Ioanne; vel quilibet beatus in caelo, qui maior est quolibet viatore» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 11, l. 2).

dr_terms: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, then is the kingdom of God come upon you (*pervenit in vos regnum Dei*).
dr_plain: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out devils, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.
vulgate_text: Si autem ego in Spiritu Dei eiicio daemones, igitur pervenit in vos regnum Dei.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 12, l. 3; ST III, q. 44, a. 1; ST I-II, q. 106, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ's exorcisms by the Holy Spirit prove that the power of God has arrived to liberate men from Satan's dominion.
spi_eng: The casting out of demons signifies the interior expulsion of sin from the human soul through the infusion of sanctifying grace.
lit_lat: «Eiicere daemones in Spiritu Dei signum est adventus regni Dei» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 12, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Pervenit regnum Dei: idest destructio regni diaboli et infusio gratiae iustificantis in cordibus hominum» (*ST* III, q. 44, a. 1).

dr_terms: Because to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven (*mysteria regni caelorum*)... When any one heareth the word of the kingdom (*verbum regni*), and understandeth it not, there cometh the wicked one...
dr_plain: Because to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven... When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, there cometh the wicked one...
vulgate_text: Quia vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum... Omnis qui audit verbum regni, et non intelligit, venit malus...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 13, l. 1; ST I-II, q. 101, a. 2.
lit_eng: Christ explains the divine mysteries of the Kingdom in parables to the disciples while concealing them from the hardened.
spi_eng: The 'word of the kingdom' is the divine seed of evangelical doctrine, which brings forth the fruit of virtue only when received in a humble and understanding heart.
lit_lat: «Discipulis manifestantur mysteria regni in secreto, turbis autem in parabolis» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Verbum regni est semen divinae doctrinae, quod per gratiam recipitur in corde fideli ad afferendum fructum bonorum operum» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 1).

dr_terms: The kingdom of heaven is likened (*Simile factum est regnum caelorum*) to a man that sowed good seed in his field... The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom (*de regno eius*) all scandals, and them that work iniquity...
