Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father (*in regno Patris eorum*).
dr_plain: The kingdom of heaven is likened to a man that sowed good seed in his field... The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all scandals, and them that work iniquity... Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father.
vulgate_text: Simile factum est regnum caelorum homini, qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo... Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, et colligent de regno eius omnia scandala, et eos qui faciunt iniquitatem... Tunc iusti fulgebunt sicut sol in regno Patris eorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 13, ll. 2, 4; ST II-II, q. 10, a. 8; ST III, q. 8, a. 3.
lit_eng: Parable of the Weeds: good seed and weeds co-exist in the field until the harvest at the close of the age.
spi_eng: Refutes Donatism: 'His kingdom' in this age is the Church Militant as a mixed body (*corpus permixtum*); at the Last Judgment, sinners are separated, and the just enter the Kingdom of Glory.
lit_lat: «Parabola zizaniorum: mixtio bonorum et malorum in agro mundi usque ad messem finis saeculi» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Regnum Christi in praesenti est Ecclesia militans continens malos et bonos; in futuro purgabitur ab omni scandalo et transferetur in regnum Patris» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 4).

dr_terms: The kingdom of heaven is like (*Simile est regnum caelorum*) to a grain of mustard seed... The kingdom of heaven is like (*Simile est regnum caelorum*) to leaven...
dr_plain: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed... The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven...
vulgate_text: Simile est regnum caelorum grano sinapis... Simile est regnum caelorum fermento...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 13, l. 3.
lit_eng: Parables illustrating the disproportionate growth of the Kingdom from minute origins to universal expansion.
spi_eng: The mustard seed is Christ and the apostolic preaching, small in humble appearance but growing into the universal Church; the leaven is divine charity transforming the whole soul.
lit_lat: «Crescentia regni ex parvo principio praedicationis ad amplitudinem universalem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Granum sinapis est Christus et fides eius, parva in humilitate carnis, sed virtute diffusa super omnia; fermentum est caritas perficiens totam mentem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 3).

dr_terms: The kingdom of heaven is like (*Simile est regnum caelorum*) unto a treasure hidden in a field... is like to a merchant seeking good pearls... is like to a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kind of fishes...
dr_plain: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in a field... is like to a merchant seeking good pearls... is like to a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kind of fishes...
vulgate_text: Simile est regnum caelorum thesauro abscondito in agro... Simile est regnum caelorum homini negotiatori, quaerenti bonas margaritas... Simile est regnum caelorum sagenae missae in mare, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 13, l. 4; ST II-II, q. 186, a. 3.
lit_eng: Parables of the Hidden Treasure, Pearl of Great Price, and Dragnet.
spi_eng: The treasure and pearl represent the contemplative enjoyment of divine truth and beatitude, for which a man renounces all earthly goods; the dragnet is the Church gathering all men until final judgment.
lit_lat: «Parabolae thesauri, margaritae et sagenae missae in mare» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 13, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Thesaurus et margarita sunt contemplatio veritatis divinae et deliciae regni caelestis, pro quibus omnia temporalia venduntur; sagena est Ecclesia colligens omnes usque ad iudicium» (*ST* II-II, q. 186, a. 3).

dr_terms: And I say to thee: That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church... And I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven (*claves regni caelorum*). And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven...
dr_plain: And I say to thee: That thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church... And I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth, it shall be bound also in heaven...
vulgate_text: Et ego dico tibi, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam... Et tibi dabo claves regni caelorum. Et quodcumque ligaveris super terram, erit ligatum et in caelis...
locus: Super Mt., cap. 16, l. 2; ST Suppl., qq. 17–20; Contra Graec. II, cap. 32.
lit_eng: Christ promises Peter ministerial stewardship, conferring the keys of authority to govern the Church Militant.
spi_eng: The keys signify spiritual power of order and jurisdiction, whereby apostolic ministers open heaven to the faithful through sacramental absolution and the removal of the debt of sin.
lit_lat: «Collatio potestatis iurisdictionis et ordinis Petro super totam Ecclesiam militantem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 16, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Claves regni caelorum sunt potestas spiritualis aperiendi caelum per absolutionem peccatorum et ministerium sacramentorum» (*ST* Suppl., q. 17, a. 1).

dr_terms: Amen I say to you, there are some of them that stand here, that shall not taste death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom (*venientem in regno suo*).
dr_plain: Amen I say to you, there are some of them that stand here, that shall not taste death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
vulgate_text: Amen dico vobis, sunt quidam de hic stantibus, qui non gustabunt mortem, donec videant Filium hominis venientem in regno suo.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 16, l. 3; ST III, q. 45, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ promises that certain disciples will behold the coming of His royal dignity before dying.
spi_eng: Fulfilled on Mount Tabor in the Transfiguration, where Peter, James, and John were granted an anticipatory vision of Christ's glorified, radiant humanity in the Kingdom of Heaven.
lit_lat: «Promissio visionis regalis gloriae Christi aliquibus discipulis ante mortem» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 16, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Impletum est in Transfiguratione in monte Thabor, ubi Christus praelibationem regni sui gloriosi Petro, Iacobo et Ioanni ostendit» (*ST* III, q. 45, a. 1).

dr_terms: Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heaven (*in regno caelorum*)? ...Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven (*in regno caelorum*).
dr_plain: Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heaven? ...Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven.
vulgate_text: Quis, putas, maior est in regno caelorum? ...Quicumque ergo humiliaverit se sicut parvulus iste, hic est maior in regno caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 18, l. 1; ST II-II, q. 161, a. 1.
lit_eng: Disciples dispute over precedence in the expected messianic realm; Christ corrects them by setting a child in their midst.
spi_eng: True greatness in the Kingdom of Grace is measured not by temporal dominion, but by innocent humility and charity devoid of pride and ambition.
lit_lat: «Correctio ambitionis discipulorum contendentium de primatu regni» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 18, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Magnitudo in regno gratiae et gloriae non attenditur secundum potentiam saecularem, sed secundum profunditatem humilitatis et perfectionem caritatis» (*ST* II-II, q. 161, a. 1).

dr_terms: Amen, I say to you, that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven (*intrabit in regnum caelorum*). And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven (*intrare in regnum caelorum*).
dr_plain: Amen, I say to you, that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven.
vulgate_text: Amen dico vobis, quia dives difficile intrabit in regnum caelorum. Et iterum dico vobis: Facilius est camelum per foramen acus transire, quam divitem intrare in regnum caelorum.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 19, l. 2; ST II-II, q. 186, a. 3.
lit_eng: Christ warns that attachment to earthly wealth makes entrance into the Kingdom of Heaven morally impossible for human power.
spi_eng: Riches entangle the affections in the earthly city; only the grace of God can detach the heart to enter the narrow portal of celestial beatitude.
lit_lat: «Divitiae sunt grave impedimentum ad ingrediendum regnum caelorum propter amorem carnalem earum» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 19, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Camelus deponens sarcinam transit foramen acus: dives debet deponere affectum divitiarum per paupertatem spiritus ut ingrediatur regnum» (*ST* II-II, q. 186, a. 3).

dr_terms: Say that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left, in thy kingdom (*in regno tuo*)... but to sit on my right or left hand, is not mine to give to you, but to them for whom it is prepared by my Father.
dr_plain: Say that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left, in thy kingdom... but to sit on my right or left hand, is not mine to give to you, but to them for whom it is prepared by my Father.
vulgate_text: Dic ut sedeant hi duo filii mei, unus ad dexteram tuam, et unus ad sinistram in regno tuo... sedere autem ad dexteram meam vel sinistram non est meum dare vobis, sed quibus paratum est a Patre meo.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 20, l. 3; ST III, q. 59, a. 5.
lit_eng: The mother of James and John seeks places of royal honor for her sons in Christ's kingdom.
spi_eng: Christ refutes carnal nepotism: heavenly thrones are distributed according to the Father's eternal predestination and conformity to Christ's Passion, not human favoritism.
lit_lat: «Petitio filiorum Zebedaei de sedibus praelationis in regno temporali» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 20, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Non est meum dare vobis: idest secundum carnalem propinquitatem; sed datur illis quibus praeparatum est a Patre per aeternam praedestinationem et meritum passionis» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 5).

dr_terms: Therefore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you (*auferetur a vobis regnum Dei*), and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof.
dr_plain: Therefore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof.
vulgate_text: Ideo dico vobis quia auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, et dabitur genti facienti fructus eius.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 21, l. 4; ST I-II, q. 106, a. 3.
lit_eng: Christ concludes the parable of the wicked tenants: the kingdom is revoked from the Jewish authorities and transferred to another people.
spi_eng: The divine covenant and stewardship of grace are formally transferred from the Old Synagogue to the Catholic Church of the Gentiles.
lit_lat: «Iudicium super principes Iudaeorum: translatio regni Dei ad gentiles» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 21, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Regnum Dei est fides et dispensatio sacramentorum ac Scripturae, quae aufertur a Synagoga et traditur Ecclesiae catholicae» (*ST* I-II, q. 106, a. 3).

dr_terms: The kingdom of heaven is likened (*Simile factum est regnum caelorum*) to a king, who made a marriage for his son.
dr_plain: The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king, who made a marriage for his son.
vulgate_text: Simile factum est regnum caelorum homini regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 22, l. 1; ST III, q. 2, a. 1.
lit_eng: Parable of the King inviting guests to the wedding banquet of his royal son.
spi_eng: The wedding feast is the Incarnation itself, wherein God the Father joined human nature to His Son, espousing the Church to Christ and calling the nations to the banquet of grace.
lit_lat: «Parabola de nuptiis filii regis et vocatione convivarum» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 22, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Pater est Deus; filius sponsus est Christus; nuptiae sunt unio Verbi cum humana natura in Incarnatione et cum Ecclesia per gratiam» (*ST* III, q. 2, a. 1).

dr_terms: And when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty (*super sedem maiestatis suae*)... Then shall the king say to them that shall be on his right hand: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you (*possidete paratum vobis regnum*) from the foundation of the world.
dr_plain: And when the Son of man shall come in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then shall he sit upon the seat of his majesty... Then shall the king say to them that shall be on his right hand: Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
vulgate_text: Cum autem venerit Filius hominis in maiestate sua, et omnes angeli cum eo, tunc sedebit super sedem maiestatis suae... Tunc dicet rex his qui ad dexteram eius erunt: Venite benedicti Patris mei, possidete paratum vobis regnum a constitutione mundi.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 25, l. 3; ST III, q. 59, a. 5; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: The General Judgment: Christ the King publicly sits upon His glorious throne, judging all nations according to works of mercy.
spi_eng: The ultimate entrance of the elect into the everlasting Kingdom of Glory, eternally prepared for them by the predestination of the Father.
lit_lat: «Iudicium universale ubi Christus ut rex iudicat omnes gentes in carne sua gloriosa» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 25, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Possidete paratum vobis regnum: introductio electorum in perfectam fruitionem Dei in gloria Paradisi secundum opera misericordiae» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: And I say to you, I will not drink from henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it with you new in the kingdom of my Father (*in regno Patris mei*).
dr_plain: And I say to you, I will not drink from henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I shall drink it with you new in the kingdom of my Father.
vulgate_text: Dico autem vobis: non bibam amodo de hoc genimine vitis usque in diem illum, cum illud bibam vobiscum novum in regno Patris mei.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 26, l. 4; ST III, q. 73, a. 5; ST III, q. 83, a. 4.
lit_eng: Christ concludes the Last Supper, abstaining from wine until the Kingdom of the Father is realized.
spi_eng: The Eucharistic banquet of the Church Militant is a pledge and type of the celestial feast in heaven, where the elect enjoy the 'new wine' of direct beatific fruition.
lit_lat: «Cessatio sacrificiorum figurativorum et veteris paschatis in ultima cena» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 26, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Vinum novum in regno Patris est novitas et suavitas aeternae beatitudinis, cuius Eucharistia est pignus et figura» (*ST* III, q. 73, a. 5).

dr_terms: All power is given to me in heaven and in earth (*Data est mihi omnis potestas in caelo et in terra*).
dr_plain: All power is given to me in heaven and in earth.
vulgate_text: Data est mihi omnis potestas in caelo et in terra.
locus: Super Mt., cap. 28, l. 3; ST III, q. 59, aa. 1–2; De reg. I, cap. 14.
lit_eng: The Risen Christ proclaims that all universal power has been conferred upon Him, commanding the Apostles to disciple all nations.
spi_eng: Christ possesses universal legislative, judicial, and executive authority over all creation according to His human nature, commissioning the Church as His visible instrument of salvation.
lit_lat: «Omnis potestas data est Christo resurgenti secundum humanam naturam, ut constituatur rex et iudex omnium» (*Super Mt.*, cap. 28, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Ex hac potestate regia mittit Apostolos ad docendum omnes gentes et fundandum Ecclesiam per universum orbem» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God (*praedicans evangelium regni Dei*), and saying: The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand (*appropinquavit regnum Dei*): repent, and believe the gospel.
dr_plain: Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, and saying: The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel.
vulgate_text: Venit Iesus in Galilaeam, praedicans evangelium regni Dei, et dicens: Quoniam impletum est tempus, et appropinquavit regnum Dei: poenitemini, et credite evangelio.
locus: Cat. in Mc., cap. 1, l. 5.
lit_eng: The Marcan kerygma: the appointed prophetic time has arrived and the Kingdom of God is inaugurated in Galilee.
spi_eng: The shadows of the Old Law cease upon the arrival of the Incarnate Truth, calling the human soul to interior penance and living faith.
lit_lat: «Impletum est tempus prophetiae et regnum Messiae incipit in Galilaea» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 1, l. 5).
spi_lat: «Appropinquavit regnum Dei: idest ipse Christus adest per carnem; poenitemini ut per fidem intretis in gratiam eius» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 1, l. 5).

dr_terms: So is the kingdom of God (*Sic est regnum Dei*), as if a man should cast seed into the earth, and should sleep, and rise, night and day, and the seed should spring, and grow up whilst he knoweth not.
dr_plain: So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the earth, and should sleep, and rise, night and day, and the seed should spring, and grow up whilst he knoweth not.
vulgate_text: Sic est regnum Dei, quemadmodum si homo iaciat sementem in terram, et dormiat, et exsurgat nocte et die, et semen germinet, et increscat dum nescit ille.
locus: Cat. in Mc., cap. 4, l. 4.
lit_eng: Parable of the Seed Growing Secretly: the earth produces fruit of itself through hidden, gradual growth.
spi_eng: The interior, mysterious operation of divine grace in the soul, where the infused virtues mature from initial conversion to perfect charity without human comprehension.
lit_lat: «Parabola de semine terrae secreto et insensibiliter crescente usque ad messem» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 4, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Regnum Dei est operatio gratiae in anima, quae a virtute divina invisibiliter nutritur a fidei principio usque ad perfectionem caritatis» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 4, l. 4).

dr_terms: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not; for of such is the kingdom of God (*talium est enim regnum Dei*). Amen I say to you, whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God (*non receperit regnum Dei*) as a little child, shall not enter into it.
dr_plain: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not; for of such is the kingdom of God. Amen I say to you, whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, shall not enter into it.
vulgate_text: Sinite parvulos venire ad me, et ne prohibueritis eos: talium est enim regnum Dei. Amen dico vobis: Quisquis non receperit regnum Dei velut parvulus, non intrabit in illud.
locus: Cat. in Mc., cap. 10, l. 2; ST II-II, q. 161, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ welcomes little children, presenting them as the pattern for entering the Kingdom of God.
spi_eng: Receiving the Kingdom as a child signifies spiritual innocence and the utter absence of malice, deceit, and worldly ambition.
lit_lat: «Christus benedicit parvulos et proponit eos in exemplum auditoribus» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 10, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Talium est regnum Dei: scilicet eorum qui habent innocentiam et humilitatem parvuli, carentes malitia et superbia saeculari» (*ST* II-II, q. 161, a. 1).

dr_terms: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God (*Non es longe a regno Dei*).
dr_plain: Thou art not far from the kingdom of God.
vulgate_text: Non es longe a regno Dei.
locus: Cat. in Mc., cap. 12, l. 4; ST I-II, q. 106, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ commends the scribe who recognized that love of God and neighbor surpasses all burnt offerings.
spi_eng: The scribe was near the Kingdom because he recognized the spiritual essence of the New Law, which prioritizes charity over external ceremonial works.
lit_lat: «Laus scribae sapienter respondentis de dilectione Dei et proximi prae holocaustis» (*Cat. in Mc.*, cap. 12, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Non es longe a regno: quia appropinquat ad legem Evangelii, quae consistit principaliter in caritate et gratia interiori» (*ST* I-II, q. 106, a. 1).

dr_terms: He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the most High; and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father (*sedem David patris eius*); and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever (*regnabit in domo Iacob in aeternum*). And of his kingdom there shall be no end (*regni eius non erit finis*).
dr_plain: He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the most High; and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of David his father; and he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever. And of his kingdom there shall be no end.
vulgate_text: Hic erit magnus, et Filius Altissimi vocabitur, et dabit illi Dominus Deus sedem David patris eius: et regnabit in domo Iacob in aeternum, et regni eius non erit finis.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 1, l. 6; ST III, q. 31, a. 2; ST III, q. 59, a. 2.
lit_eng: The Annunciation: the archangel Gabriel declares that Jesus will inherit the Davidic throne and reign over the house of Jacob eternally.
spi_eng: The 'house of Jacob' is the universal Church of believers, over whom Christ reigns not by earthly political coercion, but eternally through grace.
lit_lat: «Gabriel annuntiat Mariae regnum sempiternum filii sui in throno David» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 1, l. 6).
spi_lat: «Domus Iacob est Ecclesia fidelium, super quam Christus regnat spiritualiter in terra per gratiam et in caelo per gloriam in aeternum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: To other cities also I must preach the kingdom of God (*evangelizare regnum Dei*): for therefore am I sent.
dr_plain: To other cities also I must preach the kingdom of God: for therefore am I sent.
vulgate_text: Quia et aliis civitatibus oportet me evangelizare regnum Dei: ideo enim missus sum.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 4, l. 10; ST III, q. 40, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ states that the primary purpose of His mission from the Father is the public proclamation of the Kingdom of God to all cities.
spi_eng: Manifests that the New Law is fundamentally an apostolic, communicative doctrine meant to illuminate the minds of all humanity.
lit_lat: «Necessitas praedicationis publicae Christi in diversis civitatibus Iudaeae» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 4, l. 10).
spi_lat: «Ideo missus sum: finis Incarnationis et missionis Christi fuit manifestatio veritatis et regni Dei per praedicationem» (*ST* III, q. 40, a. 1).

dr_terms: But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his justice (*quaerite primum regnum Dei, et iustitiam eius*), and all these things shall be added unto you. Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom (*dare vobis regnum*).
dr_plain: But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you. Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom.
vulgate_text: Verumtamen quaerite primum regnum Dei, et iustitiam eius: et haec omnia adiicientur vobis. Nolite timere pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 12, l. 6; ST I, q. 23, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ exhorts the disciples to abandon anxious care for food and clothing, promising them the Kingdom of the Father.
spi_eng: The 'little flock' represents the elect Church, to whom the Kingdom of Glory is given by the sovereign, gratuitous good pleasure of divine predestination.
lit_lat: «Exhortatio ad relinquendam sollicitudinem temporalium propter regnum Dei» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 12, l. 6).
spi_lat: «Pusillus grex est numerus electorum, quibus regnum beatitudinis datur non ex meritis carnalibus sed ex beneplacito praedestinationis divinae» (*ST* I, q. 23, a. 1).

dr_terms: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation (*Non venit regnum Dei cum observatione*): Neither shall they say: Behold here, or behold there. For lo, the kingdom of God is within you (*ecce enim regnum Dei intra vos est*).
dr_plain: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say: Behold here, or behold there. For lo, the kingdom of God is within you.
vulgate_text: Non venit regnum Dei cum observatione: neque dicent: Ecce hic, aut ecce illic. Ecce enim regnum Dei intra vos est.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 17, l. 5; ST I-II, q. 108, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 14; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: Christ refutes carnal Pharisaic expectations of an earthly, visible political kingdom: *intra vos est*.
spi_eng: (1) Christ Himself (*Christus ipse*) is standing in their midst, or (2) the Kingdom is interior, consisting in the righteousness, peace, and grace of the Holy Spirit in the soul.
lit_lat: «Regnum Dei non venit cum observatione signorum exteriorum sicut regna saecularia» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 17, l. 5).
spi_lat: «Intra vos est: dupliciter intelligitur; vel quia Christus est in medio vestro; vel quia regnum Dei est iustitia et pax et gaudium in Spiritu Sancto intra animam» (*ST* I-II, q. 108, a. 1).

dr_terms: And you are they who have continued with me in my temptations: and I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom (*dispono vobis sicut disposuit mihi Pater meus regnum*); that you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom (*in regno meo*): and may sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
dr_plain: And you are they who have continued with me in my temptations: and I dispose to you, as my Father hath disposed to me, a kingdom; that you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom: and may sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
vulgate_text: Vos autem estis, qui permansistis mecum in tentationibus meis: et ego dispono vobis sicut disposuit mihi Pater meus regnum, ut edatis, et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo, et sedeatis super thronos iudicantes duodecim tribus Israel.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 22, l. 7; ST III, q. 59, a. 5; ST Suppl., q. 89, a. 1.
lit_eng: Christ rewards the perseverance of the Apostles by conferring a kingdom upon them, promising that they will dine at His table and sit on thrones.
spi_eng: Confers spiritual jurisdiction upon the Apostles in the Church Militant, culminating in their sitting as judicial assessors with Christ at the General Judgment.
lit_lat: «Christus promittit Apostolis participationem sui regni et mensae in caelis» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 22, l. 7).
spi_lat: «Dispono vobis regnum: collatio spiritualis praelationis in Ecclesia praesenti, et consessus iudiciarii in futuro super omnes gentes» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 5).

dr_terms: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom (*cum veneris in regnum tuum*). And Jesus said to him: Amen I say to thee, this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.
dr_plain: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom. And Jesus said to him: Amen I say to thee, this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.
vulgate_text: Domine, memento mei cum veneris in regnum tuum. Et dixit illi Iesus: Amen dico tibi: Hodie mecum eris in paradiso.
locus: Cat. in Lc., cap. 23, l. 7; ST III, q. 46, a. 11, ad 2; ST III, q. 52, a. 4.
lit_eng: The penitent thief on Calvary confesses the crucified Jesus as true King, asking for remembrance when He enters His kingdom.
spi_eng: Thomas marvels at the thief's faith, which recognized Christ's spiritual kingdom when His flesh was nailed to the Cross, immediately meriting beatific life in Paradise.
lit_lat: «Confessio latronis poenitentis in cruce agnoscentis Christum regem esse» (*Cat. in Lc.*, cap. 23, l. 7).
spi_lat: «Fides latronis admirabilis: vidit patientem in cruce et confessus est regem in caelo, statim beatitudinem Paradisi merens» (*ST* III, q. 46, a. 11, ad 2).

dr_terms: Speaking of the kingdom of God (*Loquens de regno Dei*)... Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel (*restitues regnum Israel*)? But he said to them: It is not for you to know the times or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power.
dr_plain: Speaking of the kingdom of God... Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel? But he said to them: It is not for you to know the times or moments, which the Father hath put in his own power.
vulgate_text: Loquens de regno Dei... Domine, si in tempore hoc restitues regnum Israel? Dixit autem eis: Non est vestrum nosse tempora vel momenta, quae Pater posuit in sua potestate.
locus: ST III, q. 55, a. 2; Super Io., cap. 6, l. 2; In Orat., pet. 2. (Super Act. deest).
lit_eng: The Risen Christ instructs the Apostles for forty days concerning the Kingdom of God, correcting their carnal expectation of an earthly Jewish empire.
spi_eng: The transition from the figurative temporal kingdom of Israel to the universal spiritual Church inaugurated at Pentecost.
lit_lat: «Apostoli post resurrectionem adhuc carnaliter somniabant de regno terreno Iudaeorum» (*Super Io.*, cap. 6, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Per adventum Spiritus Sancti translati sunt ad intellegendum regnum Dei spiritualiter pro Ecclesia et vita aeterna» (*ST* III, q. 55, a. 2).

dr_terms: They believed Philip preaching of the kingdom of God (*evangelizanti de regno Dei*)... that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God (*intrare in regnum Dei*).
dr_plain: They believed Philip preaching of the kingdom of God... that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
vulgate_text: Evangelizanti de regno Dei... quia per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei.
locus: ST II-II, q. 124, a. 1. (Super Act. deest).
lit_eng: Philip and the Apostles proclaim the Kingdom of God among Samaritans and Gentiles, confirming them in patient endurance under trials.
spi_eng: Tribulations in this life are the royal path conforming the believer to Christ's Passion, making the soul worthy of the Kingdom of Glory.
lit_lat: «Praedicatio Philippi et Pauli confirmans discipulos in patientia tribulationum» (*ST* II-II, q. 124, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Per multas tribulationes: passio est via regia qua conformamur Christo capiti ad intrandum in regnum gloriae» (*ST* II-II, q. 124, a. 1).

dr_terms: Testifying the kingdom of God (*Testificans regnum Dei*)... Preaching the kingdom of God (*Praedicans regnum Dei*), and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom, without prohibition.
dr_plain: Testifying the kingdom of God... Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom, without prohibition.
vulgate_text: Testificans regnum Dei... Praedicans regnum Dei, et docens quae sunt de Domino Iesu Christo, cum omni fiducia, sine prohibitione.
locus: ST II-II, q. 188, a. 6. (Super Act. deest).
lit_eng: Acts concludes with Paul imprisoned in Rome, unhindered in preaching the Kingdom of God and the Lord Jesus Christ to all who come to him.
spi_eng: Demonstrates that the apostolic mission terminates in the universal propagation of Christ's spiritual kingdom to the capital of the Gentile world.
lit_lat: «Paulus Romae vinculatus praedicat Iudaeis et gentibus regnum Dei et Iesum Christum» (*ST* II-II, q. 188, a. 6).
spi_lat: «Consummatio muneris apostolici: doctrina regni Dei idem est quod doctrina de mysterio Christi et fidei» (*ST* II-II, q. 188, a. 6).

dr_terms: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink (*Non est enim regnum Dei esca et potus*); but justice, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost (*iustitia, et pax, et gaudium in Spiritu Sancto*).
dr_plain: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but justice, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.
vulgate_text: Non est enim regnum Dei esca et potus: sed iustitia, et pax, et gaudium in Spiritu Sancto.
locus: Super Rom., cap. 14, l. 2; ST I-II, q. 108, a. 1, ad 1; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: Paul establishes that the New Law of the Gospel does not place the Kingdom of God in ceremonial dietary regulations.
spi_eng: Thomas's master text for the internal Kingdom of Grace: it consists in infused justice (*iustitia fidei*), peace of conscience, and spiritual joy produced by the Holy Ghost.
lit_lat: «Regnum Dei non consistit in corporalibus observantiis ciborum vel potuum veteris legis» (*Super Rom.*, cap. 14, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Sed in iustitia interiori per gratiam, et pace conscientiae erga Deum, et gaudio spirituali de bonis divinis» (*ST* I-II, q. 108, a. 1, ad 1).

dr_terms: For the kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power (*Non enim in sermone est regnum Dei, sed in virtute*).
dr_plain: For the kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power.
vulgate_text: Non enim in sermone est regnum Dei, sed in virtute.
locus: Super I Cor., cap. 4, l. 3.
lit_eng: Paul distinguishes true apostolic ministry from the rhetorical boasting of false teachers.
spi_eng: The Kingdom of God consists not in worldly eloquence (*in sermone*), but in divine supernatural efficacy (*in virtute*), converting hearts and destroying vices.
lit_lat: «Paulus redarguit vanam iactantiam falsorum doctorum qui verbis tumebant» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 4, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Regnum Dei non consistit in sermone eloquentiae humanae, sed in virtute miraculorum et gratiae convertentis corda» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 4, l. 3).

dr_terms: Know you not that the unjust shall not possess the kingdom of God (*iniqui regnum Dei non possidebunt*)? Do not err: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers... shall possess the kingdom of God (*regnum Dei non possidebunt*).
dr_plain: Know you not that the unjust shall not possess the kingdom of God? Do not err: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers... shall possess the kingdom of God.
vulgate_text: An nescitis quia iniqui regnum Dei non possidebunt? Nolite errare: neque fornicarii, neque idolis servientes, neque adulteri... regnum Dei non possidebunt.
locus: Super I Cor., cap. 6, l. 2; ST I-II, q. 88, a. 1; ST II-II, q. 118, a. 4.
lit_eng: Paul catalogues grave sins that legally exclude a person from inheriting the Kingdom of God.
spi_eng: Mortal sin immediately destroys sanctifying grace, which is the necessary title of divine adoptive sonship required to inherit the Kingdom of Glory.
lit_lat: «Peccata mortalia excludunt hominem a possessione haereditatis regni caelestis» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 6, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Peccatum mortale privat hominem gratia gratum faciente, quae est unicus titulus haereditatis regni gloriae» (*ST* I-II, q. 88, a. 1).

dr_terms: Afterwards the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father (*cum tradiderit regnum Deo et Patri*), when he shall have brought to nought all principality, and power, and virtue. For he must reign, until he hath put all his enemies under his feet (*Oportet autem illum regnare donec ponat omnes inimicos sub pedibus eius*)... that God may be all in all.
dr_plain: Afterwards the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God and the Father, when he shall have brought to nought all principality, and power, and virtue. For he must reign, until he hath put all his enemies under his feet... that God may be all in all.
vulgate_text: Deinde finis: cum tradiderit regnum Deo et Patri, cum evacuaverit omnem principatum, et potestatem, et virtutem. Oportet autem illum regnare donec ponat omnes inimicos sub pedibus eius... ut sit Deus omnia in omnibus.
locus: Super I Cor., cap. 15, l. 3; ST III, q. 59, a. 2; ST I, q. 103, a. 3; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: The final consummation: Christ abolishes all hostile powers and delivers the Kingdom to the Father.
spi_eng: Thomas explains: (1) Christ 'delivering the kingdom' means leading the redeemed to the direct vision of the Father; (2) Christ's kingship never ends, but His economic warfare ceases; (3) God becomes all in all in the beatitude of the elect.
lit_lat: «Tradere regnum Deo et Patri: idest perducere omnes fideles ad manifestam visionem Patris» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 15, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Non quod ipse regnare desinat, sed cessabit dispensatio bellica contra inimicos; et erit Deus omnia in omnibus per plenitudinem beatitudinis» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God (*caro et sanguis regnum Dei possidere non possunt*): neither shall corruption possess incorruption.
dr_plain: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God: neither shall corruption possess incorruption.
vulgate_text: Hoc autem dico, fratres: quia caro et sanguis regnum Dei possidere non possunt: neque corruptio incorruptelam possidebit.
locus: Super I Cor., cap. 15, l. 7; ST Suppl., q. 82, a. 1.
lit_eng: Paul asserts that mortal, corruptible human nature cannot inherit the imperishable Kingdom of God without transformation.
spi_eng: Mortal human nature must be transformed by the power of the resurrection into the spiritualized, impassible body of glory before entering the heavenly Kingdom.
lit_lat: «Natura mortalis et corruptibilis non potest pervenire ad statum incorruptionis caelestis sine resurrectione» (*Super I Cor.*, cap. 15, l. 7).
spi_lat: «Caro et sanguis, idest carnales affectus et operatio animalis, non ingrediuntur beatitudinem spiritualem regni» (*ST* Suppl., q. 82, a. 1).

dr_terms: Envy, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like. Of the which I foretell you, as I have foretold to you, that they who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God (*regnum Dei non consequentur*).
dr_plain: Envy, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like. Of the which I foretell you, as I have foretold to you, that they who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God.
vulgate_text: Invidiae, homicidia, ebrietates, comessationes, et his similia: quae praedico vobis, sicut praedixi: quoniam qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non consequentur.
locus: Super Gal., cap. 5, l. 6; ST I-II, q. 70, a. 4.
lit_eng: Warning that practicing the works of the flesh deprives a man of obtaining the Kingdom of God.
spi_eng: The works of the flesh extinguish charity, whereas only the Fruits of the Spirit preserve the soul in grace to inherit eternal beatitude.
lit_lat: «Opera carnis impediunt consecutivam regni Dei quia contrariantur caritati» (*Super Gal.*, cap. 5, l. 6).
spi_lat: «Fructus autem Spiritus, scilicet caritas et pax, sunt semina perducenda ad messem aeterni regni» (*ST* I-II, q. 70, a. 4).

dr_terms: For know you this and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God (*in regno Christi et Dei*).
dr_plain: For know you this and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
vulgate_text: Hoc enim scitote intelligentes: quod omnis fornicator, aut immundus, aut avarus, quod est idolorum servitus, non habet haereditatem in regno Christi et Dei.
locus: Super Eph., cap. 5, l. 2.
lit_eng: Impure and avaricious persons have no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
spi_eng: Thomas notes that the single article indicates the kingdom of Christ and the kingdom of God are one and the same: Christ's humanity leads us into the kingdom of His consubstantial divinity.
lit_lat: «Peccatores carnales et avari non habent partem in haereditate regni» (*Super Eph.*, cap. 5, l. 2).
spi_lat: «In regno Christi et Dei: una est sententia et unum regnum, quia per humanitatem Christi pervenitur ad regnum divinitatis» (*Super Eph.*, cap. 5, l. 2).

dr_terms: For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth (*caelestium, terrestrium, et infernorum*): And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.
dr_plain: For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.
vulgate_text: Propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, et donavit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen: ut in nomine Iesu omne genu flectatur caelestium, terrestrium, et infernorum, et omnis lingua confiteatur, quia Dominus Iesus Christus in gloria est Dei Patris.
locus: Super Philip., cap. 2, l. 3; ST III, q. 59, a. 1; ST III, q. 49, a. 6.
lit_eng: The Christological hymn: because Christ humbled Himself unto the death of the Cross, God exalted Him with supreme royal dignity over all creation.
spi_eng: Thomas proves that Christ merited universal royal dominion through His Passion, receiving homage from angels in heaven, men on earth, and demons in hell.
lit_lat: «Exaltatio Christi secundum humanitatem propter meritum humilitatis et passionis» (*Super Philip.*, cap. 2, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Universalis regalis potestas super angelos (caelestium), homines (terrestrium) et daemones (infernorum), qui omnes flectent genu iudiciariae eius potestati» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).

dr_terms: But our conversation is in heaven (*Nostra autem conversatio in caelis est*); from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory, according to the operation whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself.
dr_plain: But our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory, according to the operation whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself.
vulgate_text: Nostra autem conversatio in caelis est: unde etiam Salvatorem expectamus Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostrae configuratum corpori claritatis suae, secundum operationem, qua etiam possit subiicere sibi omnia.
locus: Super Philip., cap. 3, l. 3; ST I-II, q. 65, a. 5; De reg. I, cap. 14.
lit_eng: The Christian's citizenship (*conversatio/politeuma*) resides in heaven, awaiting Christ who will transform our bodies.
spi_eng: While living in mortal flesh within earthly kingdoms, the believer belongs spiritually to the heavenly city (*civitas Dei*), seeking eternal beatitude as his ultimate end.
lit_lat: «Civilitas nostra in caelis est: fideles sunt cives civitatis Dei, non civitatis terrenae» (*Super Philip.*, cap. 3, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Christus rex reformabit corpus humilitatis nostrae per virtutem qua sibi subicit omnia in regno gloriae» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love (*transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suae*).
dr_plain: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love.
vulgate_text: Qui eripuit nos de potestate tenebrarum, et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suae.
locus: Super Col., cap. 1, l. 3; ST III, q. 49, a. 1; In Orat., pet. 2.
lit_eng: God has rescued believers from the authority of darkness and transferred them into the kingdom of His beloved Son.
spi_eng: Justification is literally a spiritual translation from the tyrannical empire of Satan to the Kingdom of Christ, governed by filial love and sanctifying grace.
lit_lat: «Liberatio de captivitate diaboli et peccati per redemptionem Christi» (*Super Col.*, cap. 1, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Transtulit in regnum Filii: ipsa iustificatio est translatio spiritualis de tyrannide Satanae in statum gratiae et adoptionis filiorum» (*ST* III, q. 49, a. 1).

dr_terms: These only are my helpers in the kingdom of God (*adiutores mei in regno Dei*): who have been a comfort to me.
dr_plain: These only are my helpers in the kingdom of God: who have been a comfort to me.
vulgate_text: Hi soli sunt adiutores mei in regno Dei, qui mihi fuerunt solatio.
locus: Super Col., cap. 4, l. 2.
lit_eng: Paul identifies his fellow Jewish-Christian collaborators who labor with him for the Kingdom of God.
spi_eng: Christian ministers are 'helpers of the kingdom' because by preaching and administering the sacraments, they cooperate in gathering souls into the Church.
lit_lat: «Paulus nominat adiutores suos ex circumcisione cooperantes in praedicatione» (*Super Col.*, cap. 4, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Adiutores in regno Dei sunt omnes ministri qui per verbum et sacramenta cooperantur ad aedificationem Ecclesiae» (*Super Col.*, cap. 4, l. 2).

dr_terms: That you would walk worthy of God, who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory (*vocavit vos in suum regnum et gloriam*).
dr_plain: That you would walk worthy of God, who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory.
vulgate_text: Ut ambularetis digne Deo, qui vocavit vos in suum regnum et gloriam.
locus: Super I Thes., cap. 2, l. 2.
lit_eng: Exhortation to the Thessalonians to live a moral life worthy of God, who calls them to His heavenly kingdom and glory.
spi_eng: God summons the elect not to an earthly, perishable commonwealth, but to participate eternally in His own celestial kingship and beatific glory.
lit_lat: «Exhortatio ad sanctitatem vitae respondentem vocationi divinae» (*Super I Thes.*, cap. 2, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Vocavit vos in suum regnum: Deus non vocat ad regnum terrenum quod perit, sed ad participationem suae aeternae gloriae» (*Super I Thes.*, cap. 2, l. 2).

dr_terms: For an example of the just judgment of God, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God (*digni habeamini in regno Dei*), for which also you suffer.
dr_plain: For an example of the just judgment of God, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which also you suffer.
vulgate_text: In exemplum iusti iudicii Dei, ut digni habeamini in regno Dei, pro quo et patimini.
locus: Super II Thes., cap. 1, l. 1; ST I-II, q. 114, a. 3.
lit_eng: Present persecutions suffered by the faithful are proof of God's just judgment, preparing them to be worthy of His kingdom.
spi_eng: Patient endurance under trials merits the Kingdom of God *de condigno* through the grace of Christ, purifying the soul for celestial glory.
lit_lat: «Persecutiones praesentes sunt praeludium iusti iudicii Dei erga electos» (*Super II Thes.*, cap. 1, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Patientia tribulationum facit animam dignam regno Dei de condigno per gratiam Christi cooperantem» (*ST* I-II, q. 114, a. 3).

dr_terms: Now to the king of ages (*Regi autem saeculorum*), immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever... Who is the Blessed and only Mighty, the King of kings, and Lord of lords (*Rex regum, et Dominus dominantium*).
dr_plain: Now to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever... Who is the Blessed and only Mighty, the King of kings, and Lord of lords.
vulgate_text: Regi autem saeculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria in saecula saeculorum... Quem suis temporibus ostendet beatus et solus potens, Rex regum, et Dominus dominantium.
locus: Super I Tim., cap. 1, l. 4; cap. 6, l. 3; ST I, q. 103, a. 3.
lit_eng: Doxological confessions of God as the immortal King of ages and supreme Sovereign over all earthly potentates.
spi_eng: Christ is the 'King of kings' because all earthly princes hold power purely by participation in His sovereign rule, remaining subject to His judgment.
lit_lat: «Doxologia profitens solum Deum esse immortalem et summum principem omnium» (*Super I Tim.*, cap. 1, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Rex regum: Christus est solus potens per se, a quo omnis principatus in caelo et in terra participatur et iudicatur» (*Super I Tim.*, cap. 6, l. 3).

dr_terms: I charge thee, before God and Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead, by his coming, and his kingdom (*per adventum ipsius, et regnum eius*)... The Lord hath delivered me from every evil work: and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom (*salvum faciet in regnum suum caeleste*).
dr_plain: I charge thee, before God and Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead, by his coming, and his kingdom... The Lord hath delivered me from every evil work: and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom.
vulgate_text: Testificor coram Deo, et Iesu Christo, qui iudicaturus est vivos et mortuos, per adventum ipsius, et regnum eius... Liberavit me Dominus ab omni opere malo: et salvum faciet in regnum suum caeleste.
locus: Super II Tim., cap. 4, ll. 1, 4.
lit_eng: Paul charges Timothy in view of Christ's judicial Parousia and kingdom, expressing certitude that the Lord will preserve him for His heavenly kingdom.
spi_eng: The Second Coming (*adventus*) is the public unveiling of Christ's kingdom, which culminates in the eternal preservation of the elect in beatitude.
lit_lat: «Adiuratio Timothei coram Christo iudice venturo in adventu suo ad iudicandum» (*Super II Tim.*, cap. 4, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Salvum faciet in regnum caeleste: liberatio animae de laqueis saeculi ad indefectibilem gloriam patriae» (*Super II Tim.*, cap. 4, l. 4).

dr_terms: But to the Son: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of justice is the sceptre of thy kingdom (*virga aequitatis, virga regni tui*).
dr_plain: But to the Son: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of justice is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
vulgate_text: Ad Filium autem: Thronus tuus Deus in saeculum saeculi: virga aequitatis, virga regni tui.
locus: Super Heb., cap. 1, l. 4; ST III, q. 59, a. 2.
lit_eng: The author of Hebrews applies Psalm 45:6 directly to the Son, proving His divine nature and eternal royal throne.
spi_eng: The sceptre of equity (*virga aequitatis*) signifies the spiritual law of the Gospel, ruling souls through internal truth rather than external coercion.
lit_lat: «Thronus tuus Deus: auctor adducit Psalmum ad probandum quod Filius est verus Deus et aeternus rex» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 1, l. 4).
spi_lat: «Virga aequitatis est iustitia spiritualis Evangelii, qua Christus regit mentes per veritatem et gratiam» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 1, l. 4).

dr_terms: Thou hast subjected all things under his feet (*Omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius*)... But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour.
dr_plain: Thou hast subjected all things under his feet... But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour.
vulgate_text: Omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius... Nunc autem necdum videmus omnia subiecta ei. Eum autem, qui modico quam angeli minoratus est, videmus Iesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum.
locus: Super Heb., cap. 2, l. 2; ST III, q. 59, a. 2.
lit_eng: Psalm 8 applied to Christ: while the visible subjection of all things is not yet accomplished, Jesus is already crowned King in heaven through His Passion.
spi_eng: Crucial for thesis: Christ's kingship is fully established in right (*de iure*) by His Passion, though its manifest execution (*de facto*) awaits the final consummation.
lit_lat: «Omnia subiecisti: impletio Psalmi 8 in Christo exaltato post passionem mortis» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 2, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Nondum videmus omnia subiecta ei de facto in hoc mundo, sed de iure iam coronatus est rex in caelis» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: For he looked for a city that hath foundations: whose builder and maker is God... But now they desire a better, that is to say, a heavenly country (*meliorem appetunt, id est, caelestem*).
dr_plain: For he looked for a city that hath foundations: whose builder and maker is God... But now they desire a better, that is to say, a heavenly country.
vulgate_text: Expectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem: cuius artifex et conditor Deus... Nunc autem meliorem appetunt, id est, caelestem.
locus: Super Heb., cap. 11, l. 3; ST I-II, q. 104, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 14.
lit_eng: Abraham and the patriarchs lived as pilgrims on earth, seeking the eternal city founded and built by God.
spi_eng: Thomas emphasizes that human final beatitude cannot be found in any temporal earthly kingdom, but exclusively in the heavenly *patria* of the City of God.
lit_lat: «Patriarchae vixerunt ut peregrini in terra, expectantes civitatem aeternam» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 11, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Meliorem appetunt, idest caelestem: finis ultimus hominis non est regnum terrenum sed civitas Dei in beatitudine» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: Therefore receiving an immoveable kingdom (*regnum immobile suscipientes*), we have grace, whereby we may serve God pleasing him, with fear and reverence.
dr_plain: Therefore receiving an immoveable kingdom, we have grace, whereby we may serve God pleasing him, with fear and reverence.
vulgate_text: Itaque regnum immobile suscipientes, habemus gratiam: per quam serviamus placentes Deo, cum metu et reverentia.
locus: Super Heb., cap. 12, l. 5.
lit_eng: Contrast with Mount Sinai: while the earthly dispensation and worldly empires are shaken, Christians receive an unshakeable kingdom.
spi_eng: The Kingdom of Christ mediated by grace is immutable and eternal, summoning the Church to offer acceptable spiritual worship.
lit_lat: «Comparatio ad montem Sinai: regna terrena et vetus lex commoventur, regnum autem Christi manet immobile» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 12, l. 5).
spi_lat: «Regnum immobile est gratia Novi Testamenti et gloria caelestis, qua offerimus sacrificium Deo acceptum» (*Super Heb.*, cap. 12, l. 5).

dr_terms: Hath not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which God hath promised to them that love him (*haeredes regni, quod repromisit Deus diligentibus se*)?
dr_plain: Hath not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which God hath promised to them that love him?
vulgate_text: Nonne Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo, divites in fide, et haeredes regni, quod repromisit Deus diligentibus se?
locus: ST II-II, q. 162, a. 1; ST III, q. 40, a. 3. (Super Iac. deest).
lit_eng: James condemns partiality toward the rich, declaring that God chose the poor in the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the promised kingdom.
spi_eng: Voluntary poverty and detachment from temporal wealth dispose the soul to be enriched with supernatural faith and charity, securing title to celestial beatitude.
lit_lat: «Reprehensio acceptationis personarum: pauperes huius mundi eliguntur a Deo» (*ST* II-II, q. 162, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Paupertas voluntaria disponit animam ad divitias fidei et efficit eam haeredem regni caelestis per caritatem» (*ST* III, q. 40, a. 3).

dr_terms: For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ (*in aeternum regnum Domini nostri, et Salvatoris Iesu Christi*).
dr_plain: For so an entrance shall be ministered to you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
vulgate_text: Sic enim abundanter ministrabitur vobis introitus in aeternum regnum Domini nostri, et Salvatoris Iesu Christi.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2. (Super II Pet. deest).
lit_eng: Peter encourages growth in virtues to secure abundant entrance into the eternal kingdom of Jesus Christ.
spi_eng: Explicitly designates the Kingdom of Glory as the eternal kingdom of Christ, into which entrance is merited through perseverance in the theological and moral virtues.
lit_lat: «Exhortatio ad exercitium virtutum ad obtinendum introitum in regnum sempiternum» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Regnum aeternum est regnum Christi in gloria, ubi sanctorum beatitudo nunquam deficiet» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).

dr_terms: Nathanael answered him, and said: Rabbi, thou art the Son of God, thou art the king of Israel (*tu es rex Israel*).
dr_plain: Nathanael answered him, and said: Rabbi, thou art the Son of God, thou art the king of Israel.
vulgate_text: Respondit ei Nathanael, et ait: Rabbi, tu es Filius Dei, tu es rex Israel.
locus: Super Io., cap. 1, l. 16.
lit_eng: Nathanael confesses Jesus as Son of God and King of Israel upon experiencing His divine omniscience.
spi_eng: Christ is King of Israel not by secular rule or carnal domination, but by divine wisdom, spiritually illuminating the minds of true believers (*qui Deum vident*).
lit_lat: «Nathanael confitetur Iesum esse Filium Dei et regem Israel propter praesentiam divinae scientiae» (*Super Io.*, cap. 1, l. 16).
spi_lat: «Rex Israel est Christus regens veros Israelitas, scilicet videntes Deum per contemplationem fidei» (*Super Io.*, cap. 1, l. 16).

dr_terms: Amen, amen I say to thee, unless a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God (*non potest videre regnum Dei*)... unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God (*non potest introire in regnum Dei*).
dr_plain: Amen, amen I say to thee, unless a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God... unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
vulgate_text: Amen, amen dico tibi, nisi quis renatus fuerit denuo, non potest videre regnum Dei... nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua, et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei.
locus: Super Io., cap. 3, l. 1; ST III, q. 68, a. 1; ST III, q. 69, a. 5.
lit_eng: Christ instructs Nicodemus that supernatural rebirth through water and the Holy Spirit is the indispensable condition for seeing and entering the Kingdom of God.
spi_eng: 'Seeing the kingdom' refers to contemplation in the Church Militant; 'entering the kingdom' denotes admission to heavenly beatitude, opened exclusively by the character and grace of Baptism.
lit_lat: «Necessitas spiritualis regenerationis per aquam et Spiritum Sanctum ad videndum et intrandum regnum» (*Super Io.*, cap. 3, l. 1).
spi_lat: «Videre regnum est contemplari fidem Ecclesiae militantis; introire autem regnum est ingredi gloriam Ecclesiae triumphantis per characterem et gratiam Baptismi» (*ST* III, q. 69, a. 5).

dr_terms: Jesus therefore, when he knew that they would come to take him by force, and make him king (*ut raperent eum, et facerent eum regem*), fled again into the mountain himself alone.
dr_plain: Jesus therefore, when he knew that they would come to take him by force, and make him king, fled again into the mountain himself alone.
vulgate_text: Iesus ergo cum cognovisset quia venturi essent ut raperent eum, et facerent eum regem, fugit iterum in montem ipse solus.
locus: Super Io., cap. 6, l. 2; ST III, q. 59, a. 4; De reg. I, cap. 14.
lit_eng: Following the multiplication of loaves, the crowd attempts to force Jesus into temporal kingship; Jesus flees alone to the mountain.
spi_eng: Major thesis locus: Christ explicitly rejects earthly, temporal kingship; His kingdom is not secular (*non temporale sed spirituale*), and its public manifestation is deferred until after the redemption and judgment.
lit_lat: «Christus fugit in montem quia turbae carnaliter volebant eum constituere regem terrenum» (*Super Io.*, cap. 6, l. 2).
spi_lat: «Regnum Christi non est temporale sed spirituale; recusavit regnum terrenum ut ostenderet suum regnum differri ad tempus post iudicium» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel (*rex Israel*)... Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy king cometh (*ecce rex tuus venit*), sitting on an ass's colt.
dr_plain: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel... Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy king cometh, sitting on an ass's colt.
vulgate_text: Benedictus, qui venit in nomine Domini, rex Israel... Noli timere filia Sion: ecce rex tuus venit sedens super pullum asinae.
locus: Super Io., cap. 12, l. 3.
lit_eng: Royal acclamation of Jesus entering Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, fulfilling Zechariah 9:9.
spi_eng: Christ permits royal acclaim not for temporal pride, but to signify that His throne is the Cross, where His spiritual kingship over the Gentiles is inaugurated.
lit_lat: «Acclamatio regia turbarum in die Palmarum sedenti super pullum asinae» (*Super Io.*, cap. 12, l. 3).
spi_lat: «Non quaesivit pompam terrenam, sed thronus regni eius fuit crux, unde regnavit in gentibus» (*Super Io.*, cap. 12, l. 3).

dr_terms: Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world (*Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo*). If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would certainly fight... but now my kingdom is not from hence (*regnum meum non est hinc*). Pilate therefore said to him: Art thou a king then (*Ergo rex es tu*)? Jesus answered: Thou sayest that I am a king (*Tu dicis quia rex sum ego*). For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth.
dr_plain: Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would certainly fight... but now my kingdom is not from hence. Pilate therefore said to him: Art thou a king then? Jesus answered: Thou sayest that I am a king. For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth.
vulgate_text: Respondit Iesus: Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo. Si ex hoc mundo esset regnum meum, ministri mei utique decertarent... nunc autem regnum meum non est hinc. Dixit itaque ei Pilatus: Ergo rex es tu? Respondit Iesus: Tu dicis quia rex sum ego. Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati...
locus: Super Io., cap. 18, l. 6; ST III, q. 59, a. 4; De reg. I, cap. 14; Sent. II, d. 44, q. 1, a. 3.
lit_eng: Christ's formal confession before Pontius Pilate: His kingdom is not derived from this world and does not compete with Caesar's empire, but rules over minds through divine truth.
spi_eng: Primary thesis locus: Christ's kingdom is *in* this world as to its subjects, but not *of* this world as to its origin; it does not usurp secular authority or depose temporal rulers, but establishes spiritual authority over souls.
lit_lat: «Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo: idest non habet originem a mundo, sed de caelo; nec aufert terrenis regibus regna saecularia» (*Super Io.*, cap. 18, l. 6).
spi_lat: «Regnum Christi est in hoc mundo quantum ad subditos, sed non de hoc mundo quantum ad finem; regnat in mentibus per veritatem et iustitiam» (*De reg.* I, cap. 14).

dr_terms: The prince of the kings of the earth (*Princeps regum terrae*), who hath loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God and his Father (*fecit nos regnum, et sacerdotes*)... I John, your brother and your partner in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus (*particeps in tribulatione, et regno*)...
dr_plain: The prince of the kings of the earth, who hath loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood, and hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God and his Father... I John, your brother and your partner in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus...
vulgate_text: Princeps regum terrae, qui dilexit nos, et lavit nos a peccatis nostris in sanguine suo, et fecit nos regnum, et sacerdotes Deo et Patri suo... Ego Ioannes frater vester, et particeps in tribulatione, et regno, et patientia in Christo Iesu...
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 1; ST III, q. 22, a. 1, ad 3. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: Doxology praising Christ as *Princeps regum terrae*, who has redeemed believers by His blood and made them a kingdom and priests to God.
spi_eng: Christ's supreme kingship transcends all earthly sovereigns; by the communication of His Passion, the Church participates in His royal and priestly character.
lit_lat: «Christus est princeps regum terrae quia omnes reges ei subiciuntur» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Fecit nos regnum et sacerdotes: communicatio regalis et sacerdotalis dignitatis omnibus membris Christi per effusionem sanguinis eius» (*ST* III, q. 22, a. 1, ad 3).

dr_terms: Because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God, in thy blood, out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation, and hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests (*fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum, et sacerdotes*), and we shall reign on the earth (*regnabimus super terram*).
dr_plain: Because thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God, in thy blood, out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation, and hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests, and we shall reign on the earth.
vulgate_text: Quoniam occisus es, et redemisti nos Deo in sanguine tuo ex omni tribu, et lingua, et populo, et natione: et fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum, et sacerdotes: et regnabimus super terram.
locus: ST III, q. 48, a. 4; ST III, q. 59, a. 5. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The new song of the twenty-four elders praising the Lamb for purchasing a universal kingdom out of all nations.
spi_eng: The saints reign spiritually on earth by ruling over carnal passions and the world through virtue, prior to reigning visibly in the resurrection.
lit_lat: «Canticum novum seniorum laudantium redemptionem universalem per sanguinem Agni» (*ST* III, q. 48, a. 4).
spi_lat: «Regnabimus super terram: sancti regnant spiritualiter in praesenti dominando super motus carnales, et in futuro regnabunt in terra viventium» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 5).

dr_terms: The kingdom of this world is become our Lord's and his Christ's (*Factum est regnum huius mundi, Domini nostri et Christi eius*), and he shall reign for ever and ever (*regnabit in saecula saeculorum*).
dr_plain: The kingdom of this world is become our Lord's and his Christ's, and he shall reign for ever and ever.
vulgate_text: Factum est regnum huius mundi, Domini nostri et Christi eius, et regnabit in saecula saeculorum.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 2; In Orat., pet. 2. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The seventh trumpet: the kingdom of this world is definitively subjected to God and His Christ for ever.
spi_eng: At the close of history, all usurped temporal power, secular kingdoms, and demonic dominion are totally subjected to Christ's public and eternal reign.
lit_lat: «Vox septimi angeli: submissio omnium regnorum mundi sub potestate Dei et Christi» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 2).
spi_lat: «Factum est regnum: in fine temporis consummabitur manifestatio regni, quando omnis inimica potestas destruetur» (*In Orat.*, pet. 2).

dr_terms: Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ (*regnum Dei nostri, et potestas Christi eius*): because the accuser of our brethren is cast forth...
dr_plain: Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: because the accuser of our brethren is cast forth...
vulgate_text: Nunc facta est salus, et virtus, et regnum Dei nostri, et potestas Christi eius: quia proiectus est accusator fratrum nostrorum...
locus: ST III, q. 49, a. 1. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: Celestial proclamation that the Kingdom of God and authority of Christ have arrived because Satan is cast down.
spi_eng: The establishment of the Kingdom of God is accomplished through Christ's Passion, whereby the devil's legal claim over mankind is broken.
lit_lat: «Proiectio draconis de caelo per victoriam Michaelis et angelorum» (*ST* III, q. 49, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Regnum Dei venit per passionem Christi, qua diabolus privatus est dominio quod habebat super genus humanum» (*ST* III, q. 49, a. 1).

dr_terms: Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, O King of ages (*Rex saeculorum*).
dr_plain: Great and wonderful are thy works, O Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, O King of ages.
vulgate_text: Magna et mirabilia sunt opera tua Domine Deus omnipotens: iustae et verae sunt viae tuae Rex saeculorum.
locus: ST I, q. 103, a. 1. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The victors standing on the sea of glass sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, praising God as the King of ages.
spi_eng: The glorified saints praise God's universal royal governance across all dispensations of salvation history.
lit_lat: «Canticum Moysi et Agni confitens iustitiam operum Dei» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Rex saeculorum: Deus dicitur rex saeculorum quia eius gubernatio complectitur omnes ordines temporum et creaturarum» (*ST* I, q. 103, a. 1).

dr_terms: These shall fight with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them, because he is Lord of lords, and King of kings (*Rex regum*)... And he hath on his garment, and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS (*REX REGUM ET DOMINUS DOMINANTIUM*).
dr_plain: These shall fight with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them, because he is Lord of lords, and King of kings... And he hath on his garment, and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.
vulgate_text: Hi cum Agno pugnabunt, et Agnus vincet illos: quoniam Dominus dominorum est, et Rex regum... Et habet in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum: REX REGUM ET DOMINUS DOMINANTIUM.
locus: ST III, q. 59, a. 1; De reg. I, cap. 8; Sent. II, d. 44. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The Lamb overcomes the hostile kings of the earth because He is King of kings and Lord of lords.
spi_eng: Christ bears the title *Rex regum* because every human monarch and civil authority is subordinate to Him and holds power solely by participation in His divine lordship.
lit_lat: «Agnus vincet reges terrae quia ipse est Rex regum et Dominus dominantium» (*ST* III, q. 59, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Nomen scriptum in femore: potestas regia Christi derivatur a Patre secundum divinitatem et manifestatur in humanitate per victoriam super omnes tyrannos» (*De reg.* I, cap. 8).

dr_terms: And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years (*regnaverunt cum Christo mille annis*)... they shall be priests of God and of Christ; and shall reign with him a thousand years (*regnabunt cum eo mille annis*).
dr_plain: And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years... they shall be priests of God and of Christ; and shall reign with him a thousand years.
vulgate_text: Et vixerunt, et regnaverunt cum Christo mille annis... erunt sacerdotes Dei et Christi, et regnabunt cum eo mille annis.
locus: ST Suppl., q. 77, a. 1; ST III, q. 59, a. 5. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The vision of the martyrs living and reigning with Christ for a thousand years.
spi_eng: Refutes millenarianism: following Augustine (*De Civitate Dei* XX), Thomas explains that the 'thousand years' denotes the present era of the Church Militant, where the saints already reign with Christ through faith and grace.
lit_lat: «Visio sedium et regni martyrum cum Christo per mille annos» (*ST* Suppl., q. 77, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Refutatio chiliasmi: mille anni significant totum tempus praesentis Ecclesiae, in qua sancti regnant cum Christo per fidem et caritatem» (*ST* Suppl., q. 77, a. 1).

dr_terms: And the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it (*thronus Dei et Agni in ea erunt*), and his servants shall serve him. And they shall see his face: and his name shall be on their foreheads... and they shall reign for ever and ever (*regnabunt in saecula saeculorum*).
dr_plain: And the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it, and his servants shall serve him. And they shall see his face: and his name shall be on their foreheads... and they shall reign for ever and ever.
vulgate_text: Et thronus Dei et Agni in ea erunt, et servi eius servient illi. Et videbunt faciem eius: et nomen eius in frontibus eorum... et regnabunt in saecula saeculorum.
locus: ST I, q. 12, a. 1; ST Suppl., q. 93, a. 1; In Orat., pet. 2. (Super Apoc. deest).
lit_eng: The final vision of the New Jerusalem: the throne of God and of the Lamb, where His servants see His face and reign for ever.
spi_eng: The ultimate consummation of the biblical revelation: the Beatific Vision, wherein the glorified elect participate immutably in God's eternal kingship.
lit_lat: «Thronus Dei et Agni in Ierusalem caelesti, ubi servi eius regnant in aeternum» (*ST* Suppl., q. 93, a. 1).
spi_lat: «Videbunt faciem eius: essentialis beatitudo sanctorum consistit in visione divinae essentiae, qua beati participant regnum aeternum» (*ST* I, q. 12, a. 1).
